Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the
cited scalar operator and spectral suppliers. Fix integers $d\ge1$, $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$. Let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the
component-valued space of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]]
with its componentwise inner product, let $Q_{j}^{(1)},P_{k}^{(1)}$ be the
scalar position and momentum operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]], and let
$\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with
$\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^{1}$
([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Write
$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}:=\Psi_{0}\bigl(\bigoplus_{l}\mathcal F_{2}\bigr)\Psi_{0}^{-1}$
for its componentwise version, with $\Psi_{0}$ the unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] clause (a).
Define, componentwise,
$$D(Q_{j}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (Q_{j}f)_{l}:=x_{j}f_{l},$$
$$D(P_{k}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ D_{k}f_{l}\text{ exists in }L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
where $D_{k}$ is the weak derivative of [[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]].
Write $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the classes whose components
lie in $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]),
and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the componentwise Schwartz
class ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]). Then:

(a) under $\Psi_{0}$ the operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are the orthogonal sums
$\bigoplus_{l}Q_{j}^{(1)}$ and $\bigoplus_{l}P_{k}^{(1)}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-orthogonal-sums-of-self-adjoint-operators]]; in particular
$Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are densely defined and self-adjoint with the displayed
domains;

(b) $\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}$ is unitary,
$$D(P_{k})=\bigl\{f\in H^{(r)}:\ \xi_{k}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\bigr\},$$
and for every $f\in D(P_{k})$
$$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}(P_{k}f)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi_{k}\,\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f(\xi)\qquad\text{for almost every }\xi;$$

(c) the componentwise translation $T_{a}^{(r)}f:=f(\cdot-a)$, $a\in\mathbb R^{d}$,
is unitary, leaves $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
invariant, satisfies $D_{k}(T_{a}^{(r)}f)=T_{a}^{(r)}(D_{k}f)$ for
$f\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
$$T_{a}^{(r)}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}Q_{j}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I,\qquad T_{a}^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}P_{k}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=P_{k};$$

(d) for every $f\in D(P_{j})$,
$$\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t\bigl(T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}f-f\bigr)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}f \qquad\text{in }H^{(r)},$$
so the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}$ has generator $-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}$ and
$$T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}=\exp\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tP_{j}\Bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the exponential being the spectral-calculus flow of the self-adjoint operator
$P_{j}$.

**(a) Adopted framework assumptions.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, in the readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]], [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix real model parameters $m>0$ (mass parameter, unit $\mathrm{kg}$), $\omega>0$ (angular frequency, unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$) and the action constant $\hbar>0$ (unit $\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$) of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)4, and put
$$\ell:=\sqrt{\frac{\hbar}{m\omega}}>0\qquad\text{(unit }\mathrm m\text{),}$$
the model's length scale.

**(b) One-dimensional realization.** Write $\mathcal H_1:=L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx;\mathbb C)$ for the model's one-dimensional state space, the complex Hilbert space of almost-everywhere classes with inner product linear in the first argument, taken in the scalar reading $r=1$ of the component-valued space of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] for $d=1$. The model's **position** and **momentum** are the operators of that lemma at $d=1$, $r=1$, namely
$$Q:=M_x,\qquad D(Q)=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:xf\in L^{2}\},\qquad (Qf)(x)=xf(x),$$
$$P:=-i\hbar D_x,\qquad D(P)=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:\text{the weak derivative }D_xf\text{ lies in }L^{2}\},\qquad Pf=-i\hbar D_xf,$$
which are densely defined and self-adjoint with exactly these domains; the model assigns to $(Q,\mathrm m)$ and to $(P,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$ the status of assigned sharp observables in the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), with outcome laws read from P2.

**(c) Energy and excitation-number observables.** Let $g_0,(g_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ and the unitary $D:L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)\to L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$ be the Hermite data and scaling map of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (a), (b) for the parameters $m,\omega,\hbar$. Put $\mathscr P_y:=\{p g_0:p\in\mathbb C[y]\}\subseteq L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$; the Hermite recurrence [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-recurrence]] identifies this polynomial-Gaussian space with $\operatorname{span}\{g_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$, and its scaled image $\mathscr P_x:=D(\mathscr P_y)=\operatorname{span}\{\psi_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$ is the core supplied by the scaling theorem. Let $A$ be the diagonal operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]] for the family $(g_n)$ and eigenvalues $2n+1$. The model's **energy operator** is
$$H_1:=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\,D A D^{-1},\qquad D(H_1):=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:D^{-1}f\in D(A)\},$$
the operator of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clause (b); its exact domain, action, spectrum and eigenbasis are those established there. The model assigns to $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ the status of assigned energy observable of the isolated system in the sense of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clauses (a) and (b): the model's flow is $U(t)=\exp(-itH_1/\hbar)$ and the model's Schroedinger dynamics is the one of that definition. Let $N$ be the self-adjoint number operator on $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$ of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]] for the Hermite family $(g_n)$, and set $N_\psi:=DND^{-1}$. Its transported domain and action are
$$D(N_\psi)=\Bigl\{f\in\mathcal H_1:\sum_n n^2|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad N_\psi f=\sum_n n\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\psi_n,$$
with the series converging in $\mathcal H_1$; it is self-adjoint by [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-unitary-transport-of-spectral-pvms]] clauses (a), (d). The model assigns to $(N_\psi,1/\mathrm{count})$ the status of its dimensionless excitation-number observable; here $\mathrm{count}$ denotes one excitation count and is dimensionless, so the spectral coordinate $n$ records $n$ excitations, and its outcome laws are read by P2. On the scaled polynomial-Gaussian core $\mathscr P_x$ the operator $H_1$ is the self-adjoint realization of the quadratic expression: for every $f\in\mathscr P_x$,
$$H_1f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}f''+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}f$$
pointwise, and for every $f\in D(H_1)$ the weak identity $\int (H_1f)\varphi\,dx=\int f\bigl(-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\varphi''+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}\varphi\bigr)dx$ holds for every $\varphi\in C_c^{\infty}(\mathbb R)$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (c), (d)). The formal differential expression $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\frac{d^{2}}{dx^{2}}+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}$ is the model's **quadratic potential energy plus kinetic energy** reading; no identification of $D(H_1)$ with any independently defined maximal differential-operator domain, and no separate quadratic-form-domain characterization, is asserted.

**(d) Three-dimensional isotropic realization.** For the spinless reading $s=0$ of the massive-particle model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]], with state space $\mathcal H_3:=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dx;\mathbb C)$, position operators $Q_j$ and momentum operators $P_k$ ($j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$) with the domains and units of that definition, the model with common frequency $\omega$ has **energy operator** $H_3$ equal to the diagonal operator $H$ of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-multidimensional-oscillator-completeness]] clause (c) for $d=3$, $m_j=m$, $\omega_j=\omega$, a self-adjoint operator on $\mathcal H_3$ with the domain, spectrum and core displayed there. The model assigns to $(H_3,\mathrm J)$ the status of assigned energy observable in the reading of clause (c); its eigenbasis and the identity $H_3=\sum_{j=1}^{3}\bigl(-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\partial_{x_j}^{2}+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x_j^{2}\bigr)$ on the core are those of that theorem, and the one-dimensional realization of clauses (b) and (c) is the coordinate specialization of this one.

**(e) Physical reading and scope.** Clause (c) defines the model quantities that the page calls the energy and excitation number; it is a **model assumption** that the energy of the declared isolated particle is the assigned observable $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ and that $(N_\psi,1/\mathrm{count})$ is its excitation-number observable. The additive constant of the potential energy is removed at the minimum: for a one-dimensional potential-energy function $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^2$, with values in joules for position $x$ in metres, suppose $V$ has a non-degenerate local minimum at $0$, meaning $V'(0)=0$ and $V''(0)>0$. Taylor's theorem gives $V(x)-V(0)=\frac{1}{2}V''(0)x^{2}+o(x^{2})$ as $x\to0$; the oscillator model approximates this shifted potential-energy function by its quadratic term and sets $m\omega^{2}=V''(0)$. The oscillator's quantum ground energy in this convention is $\hbar\omega/2$. With only the stated $C^2$ regularity, the remainder is $o(x^2)$; no quantitative finite-amplitude error bound is asserted on this page (Binney §3.1, cited in the references). No measured value, no laboratory identification and no derivation of $m$ or $\omega$ from any microscopic or environmental theory is asserted. The model contains no damping, no external driving, no time-dependent parameters, no coupling to electromagnetic fields or radiation, no spin-dependent force, no anharmonic term, no relativistic correction and no boundary or many-body effect; those are separate model assumptions belonging to their own items. The parameters $m$ and $\omega$ are model parameters of dimensions $\mu$ and $\tau^{-1}$ in the conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and all displayed quantities are read in the units fixed there.

**(f) Status.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the objects used by the theorems of this page and record the readings of P1, P2, P4 and P5 in the model's terminology. They assert no preparation or apparatus model, no detection model, no joint outcome law of position and momentum and no empirical result.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following kinematics and one-particle model. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), which are the choice hypotheses of the cited operator suppliers.

**(i) Spacetime and frames.** The model reads its events and frames in the Newtonian arena of [[def-nrqm-framework-newtonian-spacetime]], with inertial frames and frame changes as in [[def-nrqm-framework-inertial-frames]]: the frame changes are the Galilean transformations of [[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]], and their composition is governed by the group law of [[lem-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations-form-a-group]]. These frames are global coordinate charts, not observer congruences and not time-varying basis fields. The parameters of a frame change are read in the units fixed by [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

**(ii) Apparatus motion.** The macroscopic constituents of preparations and apparatus are described by the classical trajectories of [[def-nrqm-framework-classical-apparatus-trajectories]]; a quantum particle of the model is not assigned a worldline between preparations and detections.

**(iii) One-particle state space.** For one particle of spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and mass parameter $m>0$, the model uses the state space
$$H_{s}:=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\widehat\otimes\,\mathbb C^{2s+1}\cong L^{2}\bigl(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1}\bigr),$$
whose second factor carries the spin representation assigned in the postulate P6, and $\hbar>0$ is the action constant of the adopted unit system. Position and momentum act on $H_s$ componentwise: for $\psi=(\psi_1,\dots,\psi_{2s+1})$ the $j$-th position acts by $(Q_j\psi)_l(x):=x_j\psi_l(x)$ on the classes with $x_j\psi_l\in L^2$, and the $k$-th momentum by $(P_k\psi)_l:=-i\hbar D_k\psi_l$ on the classes whose componentwise weak derivative lies in $L^2$; for one component these are the operators of [[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]], whose self-adjointness, domains and Fourier representation are supplied by [[lem-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-momentum-operators-self-adjoint]]. On the componentwise Schwartz space defined in the preceding mathematical realization, the canonical commutation relation $(Q_jP_k-P_kQ_j)\psi=i\hbar\delta_{jk}\psi$ holds componentwise by [[lem-nrqm-framework-ccr-on-the-schwartz-core]] ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]).

**(iv) Baseline Hamiltonian.** For a real bounded measurable potential $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ the model uses the scalar Hamiltonian
$$H_{\mathrm{op}}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta+V(Q),\qquad D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\ \text{(componentwise)},$$
with the free part $-\hbar^{2}\Delta/2m$ and the bounded multiplier $V(Q)$ as in [[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]] clauses (b) and (c) ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]); that theorem supplies the self-adjointness of each component operator on the displayed domain and the strongly continuous unitary group it generates, which the dynamics postulate P4 then reads as the evolution. The assignment of the operator $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ to a particle of mass $m$ and spin $s$ is the physical content of this clause; the mathematical properties are those of the cited theorem.

**(v) What is separate.** The model does not follow from P1-P4: the choice of the Newtonian arena, of the frame class, of the tensor factor $\mathbb C^{2s+1}$, of the operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ as position and momentum and of the Hamiltonian of clause (iv) are all adopted. Singular or unbounded model potentials (Coulomb-type, oscillator-type, boundary and point-interaction realizations) are separate model choices with their own domains and self-adjointness statements, established before use; relativistic matter, massless particles and radiation modes are not supplied by this massive-model assignment; they are adopted separately on their own pages, without a limiting construction here. No empirical identification of a particular particle species with a value of $s$ or $m$ is made or recorded here; the species parameters are empirical inputs in the sense of P6 and P7.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the framework. They assert that the model is used in the nonrelativistic regime and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by it; no numerical measurement is recorded.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

**(a) Setting.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 in the reading of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]) and the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (a), (b), (c), with parameters $m>0$, $\omega>0$, action constant $\hbar>0$ and length scale $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(g_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be the Hermite family of $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$, let $D:L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)\to L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$ be the scaling unitary and $(\psi_n)$ the scaled eigenbasis of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (a), (b), with $\psi_n=Dg_n$; let $a_\psi=DaD^{-1}$ be the transported annihilation operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]], and let $N_\psi=DND^{-1}$ be the model's assigned excitation-number observable of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clause (c), with its stated domain and unit $1/\mathrm{count}$.

**(b) The family.** For $z\in\mathbb C$ let $\psi^{(y)}_z$ be the coherent vector of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-convergence]] clause (a),
$$\psi^{(y)}_z:=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}\,g_n\in L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy),$$
the series converging in $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$, and define the model's **coherent state** with label $z$ by
$$\Psi_z:=D\psi^{(y)}_z=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}\,\psi_n\in\mathcal H_1 .$$
The family $(\Psi_z)_{z\in\mathbb C}$ is the model's **coherent-state family**, and $z$ is its **amplitude-phase label**.

**(c) Basic properties.** The following properties of the family are those established in the cited items and are recorded here as part of the definition's reading: the series for $\Psi_z$ converges and $\|\Psi_z\|=1$, so by P1 the ray $[\Psi_z]$ is a pure preparation of the model when it is declared as one; $\Psi_z\in D(N_\psi^{k})$ for every $k\in\mathbb N$; $a_\psi\Psi_z=z\Psi_z$, so $\Psi_z$ is a unit eigenvector of the annihilation operator with eigenvalue $z$; $\langle\Psi_z,\Psi_w\rangle=e^{-(|z|^{2}+|w|^{2})/2+z\overline w}$, with modulus $e^{-|z-w|^{2}/2}$ for all $z,w$, so distinct labels define distinct preparations (their overlap modulus is less than $1$, whereas unit vectors on the same ray have overlap modulus $1$) and no two members of the family are orthogonal; and $\Psi_0=\psi_0$ is the ground eigenvector of the energy operator. ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-convergence]] clauses (a), (b), (c), (d), (e), transported by the unitary $D$ of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clause (a).)

**(d) Reading of the label.** The label $z$ is dimensionless (it is a complex number, not a quantity with a physical dimension). Its amplitude is $|z|$; when $z\ne0$, its phase is the class $\arg z\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, while $z=0$ has zero amplitude and no phase label. The mathematical coherent-state series gives the quadratic-form value $\langle N_\psi\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=|z|^{2}$ for the assigned, dimensionless excitation-number observable $(N_\psi,1/\mathrm{count})$; this is the number coordinate intended by the model's P2 reading. The coherent-state evolution result shows that the preparation means of position and momentum rotate with the phase label at angular frequency $\omega$. Clause (d) records this interpretation of the label, not an outcome of measuring the label itself.

**(e) Scope.** The definition declares a one-parameter family of preparations of the one-dimensional model and fixes its notation. It does not assert that the coherent states are the only preparations with time-independent position or momentum spreads, it does not assert minimality of any uncertainty product (that is a separate result for this family), it does not construct a displacement operator, an overcompleteness relation or a resolution of unity, and it makes no measurement, apparatus or empirical claim. The two presentations of the family -- as eigenvectors of the annihilation operator, as in clause (b), and as translated ground states -- are not identified here; only the former is defined.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $m,\omega,\hbar>0$ and let $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, $D$, $\psi_n=Dg_n$, $H_{\mathrm{osc}}=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}DAD^{-1}$ be as in [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]], with $(g_n)$ the Hermite family and $a,a^\dagger,N$ the closed ladder and number operators of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]]; put $a_\psi:=DaD^{-1}$, $a^\dagger_\psi:=Da^\dagger D^{-1}$, $N_\psi:=DND^{-1}$, acting on $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$ with the transported domains, and for $z\in\mathbb C$ let $\psi_z^{(y)}\in L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$ be the coherent vector of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-convergence]] and define $\psi_z:=D\psi_z^{(y)}=e^{-|z|^2/2}\sum_nz^n\psi_n/\sqrt{n!}\in L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$. Finally set

$$Q:=M_x,\quad D(Q)=\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R,dx):xf\in L^2\},\qquad P:=\mathcal F_2^*M_{2\pi\hbar\xi}\mathcal F_2,\quad D(P)=\{f:\xi\,\mathcal F_2f\in L^2\},$$

the self-adjoint position and momentum operators ([[lem-real-ltwo-multipliers-and-unitary-transport]], [[thm-plancherel]]; the conjugation is discharged in the proof).

Then:

(a) $H_{\mathrm{osc}}=\hbar\omega(N_\psi+\tfrac12I)$ as operators, with common domain $D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})=D(N_\psi)$;

(b) the formula

$$U(t)f:=\sum_{n}e^{-i\omega(n+1/2)t}\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\psi_n\qquad(t\in\mathbb R,\ f\in L^2(\mathbb R,dx))$$

defines a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group $U$ on $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$: each $U(t)$ is a surjective linear isometry, $U(0)=I$ and $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$, and the generator of $U$ is $-\tfrac{i}{\hbar}H_{\mathrm{osc}}$, i.e. the limit $\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t(U(t)f-f)$ exists exactly for $f\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ and equals $-\tfrac{i}{\hbar}H_{\mathrm{osc}}f$;

(c) $U(t)\psi_z=e^{-i\omega t/2}\psi_{ze^{-i\omega t}}$ for all $z\in\mathbb C$, $t\in\mathbb R$;

(d) on the orthonormal basis one has

$$Q\psi_n=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}\bigl(\sqrt{n+1}\,\psi_{n+1}+\sqrt n\,\psi_{n-1}\bigr),\qquad P\psi_n=\frac{\hbar}{i\ell\sqrt2}\bigl(\sqrt n\,\psi_{n-1}-\sqrt{n+1}\,\psi_{n+1}\bigr),$$

with the convention $\psi_{-1}:=0$; consequently, for every $z\in\mathbb C$,

$$Q\psi_z=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}\,(a_\psi+a^\dagger_\psi)\psi_z,\qquad P\psi_z=\frac{\hbar}{i\ell\sqrt2}\,(a_\psi-a^\dagger_\psi)\psi_z ;$$

(e) with means $\langle Q\rangle_z:=\langle Q\psi_z,\psi_z\rangle$, $\langle P\rangle_z:=\langle P\psi_z,\psi_z\rangle$ and variances $\operatorname{Var}(Q)_z:=\|(Q-\langle Q\rangle_zI)\psi_z\|^2$, $\operatorname{Var}(P)_z:=\|(P-\langle P\rangle_zI)\psi_z\|^2$,

$$\langle Q\rangle_z=\sqrt2\,\ell\operatorname{Re}z,\quad\langle P\rangle_z=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z,\quad\operatorname{Var}(Q)_z=\frac{\ell^2}{2},\quad\operatorname{Var}(P)_z=\frac{\hbar^2}{2\ell^2},$$

so $\operatorname{Var}(Q)_z\operatorname{Var}(P)_z=\hbar^2/4$ for every $z$ (the value produced by these exact computations; no independent uncertainty-bound statement is asserted here);

(f) after the evolution, with $\psi_z(t):=U(t)\psi_z$ and $z(t):=ze^{-i\omega t}$,

$$\langle Q\rangle_{z(t)}=\sqrt2\,\ell\operatorname{Re}z(t),\quad\langle P\rangle_{z(t)}=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z(t),\quad\operatorname{Var}(Q)_{z(t)}=\frac{\ell^2}{2},\quad\operatorname{Var}(P)_{z(t)}=\frac{\hbar^2}{2\ell^2}.$$

The parameters $m,\omega,\hbar$ enter as positive real numbers and no physical identification of $Q,P,H_{\mathrm{osc}}$ with measured quantities is made.

Adopt the postulates P1 and P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable with outcome law $\mu^{A}$ in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and let $\rho$ be a preparation. Then:

(a) **Pure preparations.** Let $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ be the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$. Then the mean of the outcome law exists and equals $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, and the second moment exists and equals $\|A\psi\|^{2}$:
$$m(\psi)=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2},$$
both read in the powers of the declared unit $u_A$ of the observable. If $\psi\in D(A^{2})$, the variance is
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\psi)\bigr)^{2}d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}.$$

(b) **Variance and its hypotheses.** For every unit $\psi\in D(A)$ the variance exists and equals
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\psi}(A)=\|A\psi\|^{2}-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}=\bigl\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\bigr\|^{2}\ge0,$$
without any hypothesis beyond $\psi\in D(A)$; no appeal to a discrete eigenbasis is made.

(c) **Non-existence is possible.** The identities of (a) and (b) are conditional on membership of $\psi$ in the stated domains. If $\psi\notin D(|A|^{1/2})$ then $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\infty$, so the mean of the outcome law does not exist as a finite real number; the mean is finite exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then $\psi$ need not lie in $D(A)$. If $\psi\notin D(A)$ then the second moment $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ is infinite. In particular every preparation of the model is a unit ray or a density operator, and no preparation is equipped with finite moments automatically.

(d) **Mixtures.** Let $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ be a spectral expansion of a preparation, $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, $(u_n)$ orthonormal. In every weighted moment sum, zero-weight terms are defined to be zero before evaluating a component integral; equivalently, only positive-weight indices are summed. This applies also to component means that are undefined at zero-weight indices. Then the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite if and only if $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$, and then $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int\lambda\,dE_{A,u_n}$. For the second moment, put $M_n:=\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,u_n}$, so $M_n=\|Au_n\|^{2}$ for $u_n\in D(A)$ and $M_n=+\infty$ otherwise; a zero weight contributes zero. Then $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_nM_n\in[0,\infty]$, and it is finite exactly when every $u_n$ of positive weight lies in $D(A)$ and $\sum_{n:w_n>0}w_n\|Au_n\|^{2}<\infty$. Thus componentwise domain membership alone does not guarantee a finite mixed-state second moment. Whenever the mixture has a finite absolute first moment, the identity of clause (b) of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] gives its mean as the absolutely convergent weighted average of the component means.

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1 and P2 together with the mathematical moment results cited below; they assert no apparatus resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance and no empirical value. Whether a concrete preparation has a finite mean or variance for a concrete assigned observable is a question about the pair $(\rho,A)$ and the tested identification of the observable, not a consequence of the framework's postulates alone.

**(a) Setting.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the
observable and probability postulate P2 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned sharp observable with
declared unit $u_{A}$ and outcome law $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ in a preparation
$\rho$, in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b).

**(b) Preparation variance.** When the mean
$m(\rho):=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and the second
moment $\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ of the outcome
law are finite, the **preparation variance** of $(A,u_{A})$ in $\rho$ is
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(A):=\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\rho)\bigr)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda),$$
read in the square $u_{A}^{2}$ of the declared unit, and the **preparation
spread** is $\Delta_{\rho}A:=\operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(A)^{1/2}\ge0$, read in
the unit $u_{A}$. When either quantity is not finite the variance and the
spread of the pair in $\rho$ are **not defined**; the definition does not
extend them by $+\infty$.

**(c) Values and hypotheses.** The variance and its hypotheses are exactly
those of the moment theorem: for a pure preparation of a unit vector
$\psi\in D(A)$ the spread is $\Delta_{\psi}A=\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\|$,
equal to $\bigl(\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}\bigr)^{1/2}$
when $\psi\in D(A^{2})$; for a preparation $\rho$ the identities and existence
criteria are those of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] and
[[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]]. In particular a mean exists
exactly when $\rho$ is concentrated on the domain of $|A|^{1/2}$ in the sense
of those items, and no preparation is equipped with finite moments
automatically.

**(d) Products of spreads.** For two assigned sharp observables $(A,u_{A})$
and $(B,u_{B})$ in a common preparation $\rho$ in which both spreads are
defined, the product $\Delta_{\rho}A\,\Delta_{\rho}B$ is a nonnegative real
number read in the product unit $u_{A}u_{B}$; for a pure preparation of a unit
vector in $D(A)\cap D(B)$ it is
$\|(A-a)\psi\|\,\|(B-b)\psi\|$ with the real means $a=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$
and $b=\langle B\psi,\psi\rangle$.

**(e) Reading and scope.** The spread $\Delta_{\rho}A$ is a property of the
pair (preparation, assigned observable): it is the standard deviation of the
outcome law that P2 assigns. It is not an apparatus resolution, not a
measurement error and not a disturbance of the preparation; those are further
objects that require a declared instrument or apparatus model and are not
introduced here. Clause (b) makes no claim that a preparation realizes a
specific laboratory state, that a laboratory procedure measures $A$ with
resolution $u_{A}$, or that the spread is observed in any experiment; the
identification of an apparatus with the pair $(A,u_{A})$ is a tested
identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7.
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] fixes the units in which the
displays are read.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix integers $d\ge1$,
$r\ge1$ and $\hbar>0$, let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the
component-valued space with the componentwise position and momentum operators
$Q_{j},P_{k}$ of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]
clauses (a) and (b), with domains
$$D(Q_{j})=\{f=(f_{l}):\ x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\},\qquad D(P_{k})=\{f=(f_{l}):\ D_{k}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\},$$
and let $D_{k}$ denote the weak partial derivative
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]). Then:

(a) *Product rule.* If $f\in H^{(r)}$ has $x_{j}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
and $x_{j}D_{j}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ (the latter read
componentwise), then $x_{j}f$ lies in $D(P_{j})$ and
$$D_{j}(x_{j}f)=f+x_{j}D_{j}f;$$

(b) *The product domain.* $D(Q_{j}P_{j})=\{f\in D(P_{j}):\ x_{j}D_{j}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\}$
and $D(P_{j}Q_{j})=\{f\in D(Q_{j}):\ D_{j}(x_{j}f)\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\}$,
and their intersection is
$$D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})=\bigl\{f\in H^{(r)}:\ D_{j}f,\ x_{j}f,\ x_{j}D_{j}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\bigr\};$$

(c) *Commutator identity.* For every $f\in D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$,
$$(Q_{j}P_{j}-P_{j}Q_{j})f=i\hbar\,f;$$

(d) *Core.* The componentwise Schwartz class
$\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]])
is contained in $D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$, and (c) holds on it.

No identity of unbounded products is asserted outside $D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$;
in particular no identity is asserted on $D(P_{j})$ alone.

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the observable and
probability postulate P2 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_{A})$ and $(B,u_{B})$ be assigned sharp
observables with outcome laws $\mu^{A},\mu^{B}$ and let
$\Delta_{\rho}A,\Delta_{\rho}B$ be their preparation spreads in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]]. Let $\psi$ be a unit vector.
Whenever $\psi\in D(A)\cap D(B)$, put
$$a:=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad b:=\langle B\psi,\psi\rangle.$$
Then:

(a) **Weak form.** If $\psi\in D(A)\cap D(B)$, then the means $a,b$ are real,
the spreads $\Delta_{\psi}A$ and $\Delta_{\psi}B$ are defined, both are read in
the units $u_{A}$ and $u_{B}$, and
$$\Delta_{\psi}A\,\Delta_{\psi}B\ge\bigl|\operatorname{Im}\langle A\psi,B\psi\rangle\bigr| .$$

(b) **Robertson form.** If in addition $\psi\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$, that is
$B\psi\in D(A)$ and $A\psi\in D(B)$, then the pairing
$\langle[A,B]\psi,\psi\rangle:=\langle AB\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle BA\psi,\psi\rangle$
is defined, is purely imaginary, and
$$\Delta_{\psi}A\,\Delta_{\psi}B\ge\tfrac12\bigl|\langle[A,B]\psi,\psi\rangle\bigr| ,$$
read in the product unit $u_{A}u_{B}$; moreover the anticommutator refinement
$$(\Delta_{\psi}A)^{2}(\Delta_{\psi}B)^{2}\ge\Bigl(\tfrac12\bigl\langle\{(A-a),(B-b)\}\psi,\psi\bigr\rangle\Bigr)^{2}+\tfrac14\bigl|\langle[A,B]\psi,\psi\rangle\bigr|^{2}$$
holds, with equality in the refined bound if and only if $(A-a)\psi$ and
$(B-b)\psi$ are linearly dependent.

(c) **Bounded observables.** If $A$ and $B$ are bounded everywhere-defined
self-adjoint operators, then clauses (a) and (b) hold for every unit
$\psi\in H$ with all hypotheses automatic ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]).

(d) **Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1
and P2 and the cited mathematics. They concern the spreads of the two outcome
laws in one preparation; they introduce no joint outcome law, no apparatus
resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance of the preparation, and no
time observable. In particular no energy-time inequality is asserted, and
clauses (a)-(c) do not claim that a laboratory procedure realizes either
observable or attains the bounds; whether a concrete preparation and apparatus
realize the pair $(A,u_{A})$ and produce the spread $\Delta_{\psi}A$ is a
tested identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix integers $d\ge1$,
$r\ge1$ and $\hbar>0$, and let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
with the componentwise position and momentum operators $Q_{j},P_{j}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]. Let
$\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ with $\psi\ne0$ be a class and let
$D_{P}:=D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$ be the product domain characterized in
[[lem-nrqm-uncertainty-product-domain-commutator-identity]] clause (b). Then
there is a sequence $(\varphi_{n})_{n\ge1}\subseteq D_{P}$ with
$$\varphi_{n}\to\frac{\psi}{\|\psi\|},\qquad Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\to\frac{Q_{j}\psi}{\|\psi\|},\qquad P_{j}\varphi_{n}\to\frac{P_{j}\psi}{\|\psi\|},\qquad \|\varphi_{n}\|=1$$
in $H^{(r)}$. In particular, if $\psi$ is a unit vector, then
$\varphi_{n}\to\psi$, $Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\to Q_{j}\psi$ and
$P_{j}\varphi_{n}\to P_{j}\psi$ in norm, and consequently
$$\langle Q_{j}\varphi_{n},\varphi_{n}\rangle\to\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \|Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\|\to\|Q_{j}\psi\|,\qquad \langle P_{j}\varphi_{n},\varphi_{n}\rangle\to\langle P_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \|P_{j}\varphi_{n}\|\to\|P_{j}\psi\| .$$

A **real Hilbert space** is a real inner-product space $H$ ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]) whose induced-length metric is complete in the sense of [[def-complete-metric-space]]: every Cauchy sequence in $H$ for the norm $\|v\|=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}$ ([[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]]) converges to a point of $H$. A **complex Hilbert space** is a complex inner-product space with the same completeness property, so that a Hilbert space is exactly a real or complex inner-product space that is a Banach space for its induced norm ([[def-banach-space]]).

**The completion convention is the Cauchy-sequence one.**
[[def-banach-space]] defines completeness by convergence of Cauchy sequences, and this page keeps that convention throughout. It is weaker than $\sigma$-completeness — the assertion that every decreasing sequence of nonempty closed subsets with diameters tending to zero has a nonempty intersection. The two agree in ZFC, but Blackadar, Farah and Karagila note that the closest-point theorem on a $\sigma$-complete inner-product space is provable in ZF, whereas the Cauchy-complete form used below consumes the Axiom of Countable Choice; nothing here silently imports the stronger notion.

For vectors $u,v$ in a real or complex inner product space,

$$|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\lVert u\rVert\lVert v\rVert.$$

Equality holds if and only if $u$ and $v$ are linearly dependent, including the case in which either vector is zero.

derivations.claim: [The model's operators and the coherent formulas] By [F1] the model's $Q$, $P$ are the $d=1$, $r=1$ componentwise operators with the displayed dense domains, and both are assigned sharp observables; by [F2] each $\Psi_z$ is a unit vector with $a_\psi\Psi_z=z\Psi_z$, $\|a_\psi\Psi_z\|^{2}=|z|^{2}$ and $\|a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\|^{2}=|z|^{2}+1$. By [F3] the vectors $Q\Psi_z=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}(a_\psi+a^\dagger_\psi)\Psi_z$ and $P\Psi_z=\frac{\hbar}{i\ell\sqrt2}(a_\psi-a^\dagger_\psi)\Psi_z$ lie in $\mathcal H_1$, so $\Psi_z\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$, and the displayed coherent means and central norms hold.

[Spreads as centered norms] Let $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$ be a unit vector. By [F4] applied to the assigned observables $(Q,\mathrm m)$ and $(P,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$, the outcome-law means and variances exist and $\Delta_{f}Q^{2}=\|(Q-\langle Qf,f\rangle I)f\|^{2}=\|Qf\|^{2}-\langle Qf,f\rangle^{2}$, and likewise $\Delta_{f}P^{2}=\|Pf\|^{2}-\langle Pf,f\rangle^{2}$.

[Bound on the product domain] Let $\varphi\in D(QP)\cap D(PQ)$ be a unit vector. By [F5], $(QP-PQ)\varphi=i\hbar\varphi$, so $\langle[Q,P]\varphi,\varphi\rangle=\langle i\hbar\varphi,\varphi\rangle=i\hbar\langle\varphi,\varphi\rangle=i\hbar$ by linearity of the pairing in its first argument. By the Robertson form of [F6] applied to the assigned sharp observables $(Q,\mathrm m)$ and $(P,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$, $\Delta_{\varphi}Q\Delta_{\varphi}P\ge\frac12|i\hbar|=\hbar/2$.

[Approximating a common-domain vector] Let $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$ be a unit vector. By [F7] there is a sequence of unit vectors $\varphi_k\in D(QP)\cap D(PQ)$ with $\varphi_k\to f$, $Q\varphi_k\to Qf$, $P\varphi_k\to Pf$, $\langle Q\varphi_k,\varphi_k\rangle\to\langle Qf,f\rangle$, $\|Q\varphi_k\|\to\|Qf\|$ and the analogous momentum limits.

[Clause (a)] By step 1.1 and step 1.2 applied to the unit vector $\Psi_z\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$, the preparation variances are the central squared norms of [F3]: $\operatorname{Var}_{\Psi_z}(Q)=\|(Q-\langle Q\rangle_zI)\Psi_z\|^{2}=\ell^{2}/2$ and $\operatorname{Var}_{\Psi_z}(P)=\hbar^{2}/(2\ell^{2})$; taking square roots gives $\Delta_{\Psi_z}Q=\ell/\sqrt2$ and $\Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\hbar/(\ell\sqrt2)$, whose product is $\hbar/2$ in the unit $\mathrm m\cdot\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}=\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{2}\mathrm s^{-1}$.

[Clause (b), relation] Let $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$ be a unit vector and let $(\varphi_k)$ be the approximating sequence of step 1.4. For every $k$, step 1.3 gives $\Delta_{\varphi_k}Q\Delta_{\varphi_k}P\ge\hbar/2$; by step 1.2, $\Delta_{\varphi_k}Q^{2}=\|Q\varphi_k\|^{2}-\langle Q\varphi_k,\varphi_k\rangle^{2}$, and the limits of step 1.4 together with the continuity of the inner product [F8] give $\Delta_{\varphi_k}Q^{2}\to\|Qf\|^{2}-\langle Qf,f\rangle^{2}=\Delta_{f}Q^{2}$, and likewise $\Delta_{\varphi_k}P^{2}\to\Delta_{f}P^{2}$. Taking square roots and passing to the limit in the inequality gives $\Delta_{f}Q\Delta_{f}P\ge\hbar/2$.

[Clause (c), saturation] Fix $z$ and put $u:=(a_\psi+a^\dagger_\psi)\Psi_z$, $v:=(a_\psi-a^\dagger_\psi)\Psi_z$, both in $\mathcal H_1$ by step 1.1. Using the conjugate-linearity in the second argument, the coherent data $a_\psi\Psi_z=z\Psi_z$ and the adjoint relation $(a_\psi)^{*}=a^\dagger_\psi$ of [F2] and [F3], so that $\langle a_\psi\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=z$, $\langle\Psi_z,a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=\langle a_\psi\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=z$ and $\langle a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=\overline z$, together with $\|\Psi_z\|=1$ and $\|a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\|^{2}=|z|^{2}+1$, the four pairings are $\langle a_\psi\Psi_z,a_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=|z|^{2}$, $\langle a_\psi\Psi_z,a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=z\langle\Psi_z,a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=z^{2}$, $\langle a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z,a_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=\overline z\langle a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=\overline z^{2}$ and $\langle a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z,a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=|z|^{2}+1$, so $\langle u,v\rangle=|z|^{2}-z^{2}+\overline z^{2}-(|z|^{2}+1)=\overline z^{2}-z^{2}-1$; hence, using the first formula of [F3] and $\overline{\hbar/(i\ell\sqrt2)}=i\hbar/(\ell\sqrt2)$, $\langle Q\Psi_z,P\Psi_z\rangle=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}\cdot\frac{i\hbar}{\ell\sqrt2}\langle u,v\rangle=\frac{i\hbar}{2}\bigl(\overline z^{2}-z^{2}-1\bigr)=2\hbar\operatorname{Re}z\operatorname{Im}z-\frac{i\hbar}{2}$, because $\overline z^{2}-z^{2}=(\overline z-z)(\overline z+z)=-4i\operatorname{Re}z\operatorname{Im}z$. By [F3], $\langle Q\rangle_z\langle P\rangle_z=\sqrt2\ell\operatorname{Re}z\cdot\frac{\sqrt2\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z=2\hbar\operatorname{Re}z\operatorname{Im}z$, so $\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=\langle Q\Psi_z,P\Psi_z\rangle-\langle Q\rangle_z\langle P\rangle_z=-\frac{i\hbar}{2}$. Therefore $\operatorname{Re}\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=0$ and $|\langle x_z,y_z\rangle|=\hbar/2$, while step 2.1 gives $\|x_z\|\,\|y_z\|=\Delta_{\Psi_z}Q\,\Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\hbar/2$, so equality holds in the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality of [F8] and $x_z,y_z$ are linearly dependent.

[Clause (b), minimality] By step 2.2 every unit vector in $D(Q)\cap D(P)$ has spread product at least $\hbar/2$, and by step 2.1 every coherent preparation attains the value $\hbar/2$; hence the minimum of the spread product over the unit vectors of the common domain is $\hbar/2$, attained by each $[\Psi_z]$.

[Clause (d)] The spread values and the relation were obtained from the model's assigned observables, the preparation-moment theorem, the product-domain commutator, the cutoff approximation and the Robertson relation; the saturation computation used the same operators and the exact coherent-state quantities. No joint outcome law, apparatus resolution, disturbance, dynamics or empirical value entered, and the identification of a laboratory pair with $(Q,P)$ is a tested identification under P7. This is clause (d).

citations.quote:
**(a) Adopted framework assumptions.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, in the readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]], [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix real model parameters $m>0$ (mass parameter, unit $\mathrm{kg}$), $\omega>0$ (angular frequency, unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$) and the action constant $\hbar>0$ (unit $\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$) of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)4, and put
$$\ell:=\sqrt{\frac{\hbar}{m\omega}}>0\qquad\text{(unit }\mathrm m\text{),}$$
the model's length scale.

**(b) One-dimensional realization.** Write $\mathcal H_1:=L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx;\mathbb C)$ for the model's one-dimensional state space, the complex Hilbert space of almost-everywhere classes with inner product linear in the first argument, taken in the scalar reading $r=1$ of the component-valued space of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] for $d=1$. The model's **position** and **momentum** are the operators of that lemma at $d=1$, $r=1$, namely
$$Q:=M_x,\qquad D(Q)=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:xf\in L^{2}\},\qquad (Qf)(x)=xf(x),$$
$$P:=-i\hbar D_x,\qquad D(P)=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:\text{the weak derivative }D_xf\text{ lies in }L^{2}\},\qquad Pf=-i\hbar D_xf,$$
which are densely defined and self-adjoint with exactly these domains; the model assigns to $(Q,\mathrm m)$ and to $(P,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$ the status of assigned sharp observables in the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), with outcome laws read from P2.

**(c) Energy and excitation-number observables.** Let $g_0,(g_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ and the unitary $D:L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)\to L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$ be the Hermite data and scaling map of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (a), (b) for the parameters $m,\omega,\hbar$. Put $\mathscr P_y:=\{p g_0:p\in\mathbb C[y]\}\subseteq L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$; the Hermite recurrence [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-recurrence]] identifies this polynomial-Gaussian space with $\operatorname{span}\{g_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$, and its scaled image $\mathscr P_x:=D(\mathscr P_y)=\operatorname{span}\{\psi_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$ is the core supplied by the scaling theorem. Let $A$ be the diagonal operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]] for the family $(g_n)$ and eigenvalues $2n+1$. The model's **energy operator** is
$$H_1:=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\,D A D^{-1},\qquad D(H_1):=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:D^{-1}f\in D(A)\},$$
the operator of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clause (b); its exact domain, action, spectrum and eigenbasis are those established there. The model assigns to $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ the status of assigned energy observable of the isolated system in the sense of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clauses (a) and (b): the model's flow is $U(t)=\exp(-itH_1/\hbar)$ and the model's Schroedinger dynamics is the one of that definition. Let $N$ be the self-adjoint number operator on $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$ of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]] for the Hermite family $(g_n)$, and set $N_\psi:=DND^{-1}$. Its transported domain and action are
$$D(N_\psi)=\Bigl\{f\in\mathcal H_1:\sum_n n^2|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad N_\psi f=\sum_n n\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\psi_n,$$
with the series converging in $\mathcal H_1$; it is self-adjoint by [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-unitary-transport-of-spectral-pvms]] clauses (a), (d). The model assigns to $(N_\psi,1/\mathrm{count})$ the status of its dimensionless excitation-number observable; here $\mathrm{count}$ denotes one excitation count and is dimensionless, so the spectral coordinate $n$ records $n$ excitations, and its outcome laws are read by P2. On the scaled polynomial-Gaussian core $\mathscr P_x$ the operator $H_1$ is the self-adjoint realization of the quadratic expression: for every $f\in\mathscr P_x$,
$$H_1f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}f''+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}f$$
pointwise, and for every $f\in D(H_1)$ the weak identity $\int (H_1f)\varphi\,dx=\int f\bigl(-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\varphi''+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}\varphi\bigr)dx$ holds for every $\varphi\in C_c^{\infty}(\mathbb R)$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (c), (d)). The formal differential expression $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\frac{d^{2}}{dx^{2}}+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}$ is the model's **quadratic potential energy plus kinetic energy** reading; no identification of $D(H_1)$ with any independently defined maximal differential-operator domain, and no separate quadratic-form-domain characterization, is asserted.

**(d) Three-dimensional isotropic realization.** For the spinless reading $s=0$ of the massive-particle model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]], with state space $\mathcal H_3:=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dx;\mathbb C)$, position operators $Q_j$ and momentum operators $P_k$ ($j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$) with the domains and units of that definition, the model with common frequency $\omega$ has **energy operator** $H_3$ equal to the diagonal operator $H$ of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-multidimensional-oscillator-completeness]] clause (c) for $d=3$, $m_j=m$, $\omega_j=\omega$, a self-adjoint operator on $\mathcal H_3$ with the domain, spectrum and core displayed there. The model assigns to $(H_3,\mathrm J)$ the status of assigned energy observable in the reading of clause (c); its eigenbasis and the identity $H_3=\sum_{j=1}^{3}\bigl(-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\partial_{x_j}^{2}+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x_j^{2}\bigr)$ on the core are those of that theorem, and the one-dimensional realization of clauses (b) and (c) is the coordinate specialization of this one.

**(e) Physical reading and scope.** Clause (c) defines the model quantities that the page calls the energy and excitation number; it is a **model assumption** that the energy of the declared isolated particle is the assigned observable $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ and that $(N_\psi,1/\mathrm{count})$ is its excitation-number observable. The additive constant of the potential energy is removed at the minimum: for a one-dimensional potential-energy function $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^2$, with values in joules for position $x$ in metres, suppose $V$ has a non-degenerate local minimum at $0$, meaning $V'(0)=0$ and $V''(0)>0$. Taylor's theorem gives $V(x)-V(0)=\frac{1}{2}V''(0)x^{2}+o(x^{2})$ as $x\to0$; the oscillator model approximates this shifted potential-energy function by its quadratic term and sets $m\omega^{2}=V''(0)$. The oscillator's quantum ground energy in this convention is $\hbar\omega/2$. With only the stated $C^2$ regularity, the remainder is $o(x^2)$; no quantitative finite-amplitude error bound is asserted on this page (Binney §3.1, cited in the references). No measured value, no laboratory identification and no derivation of $m$ or $\omega$ from any microscopic or environmental theory is asserted. The model contains no damping, no external driving, no time-dependent parameters, no coupling to electromagnetic fields or radiation, no spin-dependent force, no anharmonic term, no relativistic correction and no boundary or many-body effect; those are separate model assumptions belonging to their own items. The parameters $m$ and $\omega$ are model parameters of dimensions $\mu$ and $\tau^{-1}$ in the conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and all displayed quantities are read in the units fixed there.

**(f) Status.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the objects used by the theorems of this page and record the readings of P1, P2, P4 and P5 in the model's terminology. They assert no preparation or apparatus model, no detection model, no joint outcome law of position and momentum and no empirical result.

**(a) Assigned energy observable.** Adopt the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4) for a declared isolated system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned energy observable** of the system is an assigned sharp observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ in the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), whose declared unit $u_H$ is an energy unit in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] (joules in the SI conventions fixed there). Thus $H_{\mathrm{op}}:D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subset H\to H$ is densely defined and self-adjoint ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]), with spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$ under the choice hypotheses of [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and its outcome law in a preparation is the law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). The assignment of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is part of the model specification, as in clause (i) of P4; this definition asserts nothing about which laboratory quantity of a concrete system realizes it.

**(b) The unitary flow.** The **time evolution** or **flow** of the isolated system is the family
$$U(t):=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr):=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_H(\lambda)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P4 in the spectral calculus of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]); here $\hbar>0$ is the reduced Planck constant with its value and unit fixed by [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], so that $tH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ is dimensionless. Equivalently, $U(t)=e^{itT}$ for the self-adjoint generator $T:=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ with $D(T)=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$; the two readings agree by the uniqueness of the generator in Stone's theorem, and by [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]] ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]] clause (a)) the family $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group: $U(0)=I$, $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$, $U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]).

**(c) Schroedinger picture.** The **Schroedinger-picture evolution** of a preparation is fixed by clause (iii) of P4. A state vector evolves by $\psi(t):=U(t)\psi(0)$ for every $\psi(0)\in H$, and the **state at time $t$** of the pure preparation $[\psi(0)]$ is the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$, which is well defined because $U(t)$ is injective; a general preparation $\rho$, that is an element of the state space $D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], evolves by
$$\rho(t):=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*},$$
the reading of clause (iii) of P4 in the density-operator vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] ([[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]). In this picture the assigned observables are held fixed at their assigned values and the preparation moves.

**(d) Heisenberg picture.** For a **bounded** assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ — that is, an assigned sharp observable with $A\in\mathcal B(H)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]), so that $A$ is self-adjoint and everywhere defined — the **Heisenberg representative** of $(A,u_A)$ at time $t$ is the pair $(A_H(t),u_A)$ with the same declared unit and
$$A_H(t):=U(t)^{*}AU(t)=U(-t)AU(t).$$
By [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]] clauses (a) and (d), $A_H(t)$ is again bounded and self-adjoint with spectral projection-valued measure $E_{A_H(t)}(B)=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)$, so $(A_H(t),u_A)$ is again an assigned sharp observable of the framework; in this picture the preparation is held fixed at its value at time $0$ and the observables move. The two pictures are two bookkeeping devices for the same model; the statement that they assign the same outcome laws is proved in the Heisenberg-picture theorem of this page, not assumed here.

**(e) Stationary preparations.** A preparation $\rho\in D(H)$ is **stationary** for the assigned energy observable when $\rho(t)=\rho$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. A pure preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary when $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for every $t$, that is, when the evolved vector remains in the ray of $\psi$; the characterization of this condition by the eigenrays of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is proved in the stationary-states theorem of this page, not assumed here. An **energy eigenstate** is a pure preparation of a unit eigenvector of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$, and a **stationary state** in the model is a stationary pure preparation; by that theorem the two notions coincide.

**(f) Energy-compatible observables.** An assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ is **compatible with the energy**, or **energy-compatible**, when its spectral projection-valued measure and that of the energy commute strongly,
$$E_A(B)E_H(C)=E_H(C)E_A(B)\qquad\text{for all Borel }B,C\subseteq\mathbb R .$$
This is an equality of bounded operators on $H$, not a relation between formal commutators on a small domain; the phrase **conserved quantity** for an energy-compatible assigned observable is a claim about the time invariance of its outcome law and is established in the energy-conservation theorem of this page for bounded $A$.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P4 together with P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P4, P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematics, assert no dynamics for a prescribed time-dependent family or for an open system (clauses (iv) and (v) of P4 are separate model assumptions treated on their own pages), assert no measurement model, no apparatus realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any laboratory system is exactly isolated.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following statement of isolated autonomous dynamics. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), which are the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral and group suppliers.

**(i) Energy operator.** An **isolated autonomous system** of the sector has a declared **energy operator** $H_{\mathrm{op}}:D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subset H\to H$ that is self-adjoint ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]) and a declared energy unit in which its spectral coordinate is read. The energy operator is part of the model specification of the system; for a massive particle it is fixed by the kinematics postulate P5, and singular or unbounded model Hamiltonians require their own self-adjointness statements.

**(ii) Evolution.** The time evolution of the model is the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$$U(t):=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),\qquad U(t+s)=U(t)U(s),\quad U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1},$$
defined by the spectral calculus of the self-adjoint generator ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]], [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]], [[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]). The energy unit enters the argument of the exponential so that $H_{\mathrm{op}}t/\hbar$ acts in the dimensionless spectral variable.

**(iii) State evolution.** A vector state evolves continuously, $\psi(t):=U(t)\psi(0)$ for every $\psi(0)\in H$, and the Schroedinger equation
$$i\hbar\,\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(t)$$
holds in the norm-differentiable sense exactly for initial vectors $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$, where the derivative is the norm limit of the difference quotients; for other vectors the equation is not asserted, although the evolution remains continuous. A density-operator preparation evolves as $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$, which is a density operator for every $t$ and satisfies $\operatorname{tr}\rho(t)=1$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]).

**(iv) Time-dependent families.** A prescribed time-dependent family $t\mapsto H(t)$ of self-adjoint operators is a different model assumption: a norm-continuous finite-dimensional Hermitian family is used only through the unitary two-time propagator that its family defines, and the exponential of the integral of $H(t)$ is not identified with that propagator unless the family commutes with itself at different times. The general unbounded time-dependent case requires a separate existence and domain theorem of its own and is not adopted by this postulate; the driven-dynamics page states its own assumptions for the models it treats.

**(v) Open systems.** A non-unitary evolution of the reduced description of a system coupled to an environment is an extension obtained from an explicitly chosen environment model and a declared reduction, not a replacement for clause (ii); no environment model is adopted by this postulate.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the isolated-system idealization. They assert nothing about the origin of the energy operator of a concrete system, about the accuracy of the idealization for a laboratory preparation, or about which laboratory interactions realize an isolated evolution; those are tested identifications in the sense of P7.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $m,\omega,\hbar>0$ and let $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, $D$, $\psi_n=Dg_n$, $H_{\mathrm{osc}}=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}DAD^{-1}$ be as in [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]], with $(g_n)$ the Hermite family and $a,a^\dagger,N$ the closed ladder and number operators of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]]; put $a_\psi:=DaD^{-1}$, $a^\dagger_\psi:=Da^\dagger D^{-1}$, $N_\psi:=DND^{-1}$, acting on $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$ with the transported domains, and for $z\in\mathbb C$ let $\psi_z^{(y)}\in L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$ be the coherent vector of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-convergence]] and define $\psi_z:=D\psi_z^{(y)}=e^{-|z|^2/2}\sum_nz^n\psi_n/\sqrt{n!}\in L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$. $$Q:=M_x,\quad D(Q)=\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R,dx):xf\in L^2\},\qquad P:=\mathcal F_2^*M_{2\pi\hbar\xi}\mathcal F_2,\quad D(P)=\{f:\xi\,\mathcal F_2f\in L^2\},$$

the self-adjoint position and momentum operators ([[lem-real-ltwo-multipliers-and-unitary-transport]], [[thm-plancherel]]; the conjugation is discharged in the proof).

$$U(t)f:=\sum_{n}e^{-i\omega(n+1/2)t}\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\psi_n\qquad(t\in\mathbb R,\ f\in L^2(\mathbb R,dx))$$

defines a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group $U$ on $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$: each $U(t)$ is a surjective linear isometry, $U(0)=I$ and $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$, and the generator of $U$ is $-\tfrac{i}{\hbar}H_{\mathrm{osc}}$, i.e. the limit $\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t(U(t)f-f)$ exists exactly for $f\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ and equals $-\tfrac{i}{\hbar}H_{\mathrm{osc}}f$;

$$\langle Q\rangle_{z(t)}=\sqrt2\,\ell\operatorname{Re}z(t),\quad\langle P\rangle_{z(t)}=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z(t),\quad\operatorname{Var}(Q)_{z(t)}=\frac{\ell^2}{2},\quad\operatorname{Var}(P)_{z(t)}=\frac{\hbar^2}{2\ell^2}.$$

The parameters $m,\omega,\hbar$ enter as positive real numbers and no physical identification of $Q,P,H_{\mathrm{osc}}$ with measured quantities is made.

**(a) Adopted framework assumptions.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, in the readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]], [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]). $$\ell:=\sqrt{\frac{\hbar}{m\omega}}>0\qquad\text{(unit }\mathrm m\text{),}$$
the model's length scale.

The model's **position** and **momentum** are the operators of that lemma at $d=1$, $r=1$, namely
$$Q:=M_x,\qquad D(Q)=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:xf\in L^{2}\},\qquad (Qf)(x)=xf(x),$$
$$P:=-i\hbar D_x,\qquad D(P)=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:\text{the weak derivative }D_xf\text{ lies in }L^{2}\},\qquad Pf=-i\hbar D_xf,$$
which are densely defined and self-adjoint with exactly these domains; the model assigns to $(Q,\mathrm m)$ and to $(P,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$ the status of assigned sharp observables in the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), with outcome laws read from P2.

$$H_1:=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\,D A D^{-1},\qquad D(H_1):=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:D^{-1}f\in D(A)\},$$
the operator of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clause (b); its exact domain, action, spectrum and eigenbasis are those established there. The model assigns to $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ the status of assigned energy observable of the isolated system in the sense of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clauses (a) and (b): the model's flow is $U(t)=\exp(-itH_1/\hbar)$ and the model's Schroedinger dynamics is the one of that definition. Its transported domain and action are
$$D(N_\psi)=\Bigl\{f\in\mathcal H_1:\sum_n n^2|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad N_\psi f=\sum_n n\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\psi_n,$$
with the series converging in $\mathcal H_1$; it is self-adjoint by [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-unitary-transport-of-spectral-pvms]] clauses (a), (d). The model assigns to $(N_\psi,1/\mathrm{count})$ the status of its dimensionless excitation-number observable; here $\mathrm{count}$ denotes one excitation count and is dimensionless, so the spectral coordinate $n$ records $n$ excitations, and its outcome laws are read by P2. On the scaled polynomial-Gaussian core $\mathscr P_x$ the operator $H_1$ is the self-adjoint realization of the quadratic expression: for every $f\in\mathscr P_x$,
$$H_1f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}f''+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}f$$
pointwise, and for every $f\in D(H_1)$ the weak identity $\int (H_1f)\varphi\,dx=\int f\bigl(-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\varphi''+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}\varphi\bigr)dx$ holds for every $\varphi\in C_c^{\infty}(\mathbb R)$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (c), (d)). The formal differential expression $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\frac{d^{2}}{dx^{2}}+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}$ is the model's **quadratic potential energy plus kinetic energy** reading; no identification of $D(H_1)$ with any independently defined maximal differential-operator domain, and no separate quadratic-form-domain characterization, is asserted.

**(d) Three-dimensional isotropic realization.** For the spinless reading $s=0$ of the massive-particle model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]], with state space $\mathcal H_3:=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dx;\mathbb C)$, position operators $Q_j$ and momentum operators $P_k$ ($j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$) with the domains and units of that definition, the model with common frequency $\omega$ has **energy operator** $H_3$ equal to the diagonal operator $H$ of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-multidimensional-oscillator-completeness]] clause (c) for $d=3$, $m_j=m$, $\omega_j=\omega$, a self-adjoint operator on $\mathcal H_3$ with the domain, spectrum and core displayed there. The model assigns to $(H_3,\mathrm J)$ the status of assigned energy observable in the reading of clause (c); its eigenbasis and the identity $H_3=\sum_{j=1}^{3}\bigl(-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\partial_{x_j}^{2}+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x_j^{2}\bigr)$ on the core are those of that theorem, and the one-dimensional realization of clauses (b) and (c) is the coordinate specialization of this one.

**(e) Physical reading and scope.** Clause (c) defines the model quantities that the page calls the energy and excitation number; it is a **model assumption** that the energy of the declared isolated particle is the assigned observable $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ and that $(N_\psi,1/\mathrm{count})$ is its excitation-number observable. The additive constant of the potential energy is removed at the minimum: for a one-dimensional potential-energy function $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^2$, with values in joules for position $x$ in metres, suppose $V$ has a non-degenerate local minimum at $0$, meaning $V'(0)=0$ and $V''(0)>0$. Taylor's theorem gives $V(x)-V(0)=\frac{1}{2}V''(0)x^{2}+o(x^{2})$ as $x\to0$; the oscillator model approximates this shifted potential-energy function by its quadratic term and sets $m\omega^{2}=V''(0)$. The oscillator's quantum ground energy in this convention is $\hbar\omega/2$. With only the stated $C^2$ regularity, the remainder is $o(x^2)$; no quantitative finite-amplitude error bound is asserted on this page (Binney §3.1, cited in the references). No measured value, no laboratory identification and no derivation of $m$ or $\omega$ from any microscopic or environmental theory is asserted. The model contains no damping, no external driving, no time-dependent parameters, no coupling to electromagnetic fields or radiation, no spin-dependent force, no anharmonic term, no relativistic correction and no boundary or many-body effect; those are separate model assumptions belonging to their own items. The parameters $m$ and $\omega$ are model parameters of dimensions $\mu$ and $\tau^{-1}$ in the conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and all displayed quantities are read in the units fixed there.

**(f) Status.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the objects used by the theorems of this page and record the readings of P1, P2, P4 and P5 in the model's terminology. They assert no preparation or apparatus model, no detection model, no joint outcome law of position and momentum and no empirical result.

**(a) Setting.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 in the reading of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]) and the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (a), (b), (c), with parameters $m>0$, $\omega>0$, action constant $\hbar>0$ and length scale $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$. Let $(g_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be the Hermite family of $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$, let $D:L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)\to L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$ be the scaling unitary and $(\psi_n)$ the scaled eigenbasis of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (a), (b), with $\psi_n=Dg_n$; let $a_\psi=DaD^{-1}$ be the transported annihilation operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]], and let $N_\psi=DND^{-1}$ be the model's assigned excitation-number observable of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clause (c), with its stated domain and unit $1/\mathrm{count}$.
