$$\psi^{(y)}_z:=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}\,g_n\in L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy),$$
the series converging in $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$, and define the model's **coherent state** with label $z$ by
$$\Psi_z:=D\psi^{(y)}_z=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}\,\psi_n\in\mathcal H_1 .$$
The family $(\Psi_z)_{z\in\mathbb C}$ is the model's **coherent-state family**, and $z$ is its **amplitude-phase label**.

**(c) Basic properties.** The following properties of the family are those established in the cited items and are recorded here as part of the definition's reading: the series for $\Psi_z$ converges and $\|\Psi_z\|=1$, so by P1 the ray $[\Psi_z]$ is a pure preparation of the model when it is declared as one; $\Psi_z\in D(N_\psi^{k})$ for every $k\in\mathbb N$; $a_\psi\Psi_z=z\Psi_z$, so $\Psi_z$ is a unit eigenvector of the annihilation operator with eigenvalue $z$; $\langle\Psi_z,\Psi_w\rangle=e^{-(|z|^{2}+|w|^{2})/2+z\overline w}$, with modulus $e^{-|z-w|^{2}/2}$ for all $z,w$, so distinct labels define distinct preparations (their overlap modulus is less than $1$, whereas unit vectors on the same ray have overlap modulus $1$) and no two members of the family are orthogonal; and $\Psi_0=\psi_0$ is the ground eigenvector of the energy operator. ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-convergence]] clauses (a), (b), (c), (d), (e), transported by the unitary $D$ of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clause (a).)

**(d) Reading of the label.** The label $z$ is dimensionless (it is a complex number, not a quantity with a physical dimension). Its amplitude is $|z|$; when $z\ne0$, its phase is the class $\arg z\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, while $z=0$ has zero amplitude and no phase label. The mathematical coherent-state series gives the quadratic-form value $\langle N_\psi\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=|z|^{2}$ for the assigned, dimensionless excitation-number observable $(N_\psi,1/\mathrm{count})$; this is the number coordinate intended by the model's P2 reading. The coherent-state evolution result shows that the preparation means of position and momentum rotate with the phase label at angular frequency $\omega$. Clause (d) records this interpretation of the label, not an outcome of measuring the label itself.

**(e) Scope.** The definition declares a one-parameter family of preparations of the one-dimensional model and fixes its notation. It does not assert that the coherent states are the only preparations with time-independent position or momentum spreads, it does not assert minimality of any uncertainty product (that is a separate result for this family), it does not construct a displacement operator, an overcompleteness relation or a resolution of unity, and it makes no measurement, apparatus or empirical claim. The two presentations of the family -- as eigenvectors of the annihilation operator, as in clause (b), and as translated ground states -- are not identified here; only the former is defined.

Adopt the postulates P1 and P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable with outcome law $\mu^{A}$ in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and let $\rho$ be a preparation. Then:

(a) **Pure preparations.** Let $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ be the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$. Then the mean of the outcome law exists and equals $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, and the second moment exists and equals $\|A\psi\|^{2}$:
$$m(\psi)=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2},$$
both read in the powers of the declared unit $u_A$ of the observable. If $\psi\in D(A^{2})$, the variance is
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\psi)\bigr)^{2}d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}.$$

(b) **Variance and its hypotheses.** For every unit $\psi\in D(A)$ the variance exists and equals
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\psi}(A)=\|A\psi\|^{2}-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}=\bigl\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\bigr\|^{2}\ge0,$$
without any hypothesis beyond $\psi\in D(A)$; no appeal to a discrete eigenbasis is made.

(c) **Non-existence is possible.** The identities of (a) and (b) are conditional on membership of $\psi$ in the stated domains. If $\psi\notin D(|A|^{1/2})$ then $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\infty$, so the mean of the outcome law does not exist as a finite real number; the mean is finite exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then $\psi$ need not lie in $D(A)$. If $\psi\notin D(A)$ then the second moment $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ is infinite. In particular every preparation of the model is a unit ray or a density operator, and no preparation is equipped with finite moments automatically.

(d) **Mixtures.** Let $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ be a spectral expansion of a preparation, $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, $(u_n)$ orthonormal. In every weighted moment sum, zero-weight terms are defined to be zero before evaluating a component integral; equivalently, only positive-weight indices are summed. This applies also to component means that are undefined at zero-weight indices. Then the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite if and only if $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$, and then $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int\lambda\,dE_{A,u_n}$. For the second moment, put $M_n:=\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,u_n}$, so $M_n=\|Au_n\|^{2}$ for $u_n\in D(A)$ and $M_n=+\infty$ otherwise; a zero weight contributes zero. Then $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_nM_n\in[0,\infty]$, and it is finite exactly when every $u_n$ of positive weight lies in $D(A)$ and $\sum_{n:w_n>0}w_n\|Au_n\|^{2}<\infty$. Thus componentwise domain membership alone does not guarantee a finite mixed-state second moment. Whenever the mixture has a finite absolute first moment, the identity of clause (b) of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] gives its mean as the absolutely convergent weighted average of the component means.

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1 and P2 together with the mathematical moment results cited below; they assert no apparatus resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance and no empirical value. Whether a concrete preparation has a finite mean or variance for a concrete assigned observable is a question about the pair $(\rho,A)$ and the tested identification of the observable, not a consequence of the framework's postulates alone.

(c) **Energy outcome law.** For every unit $f\in\mathcal H_1$ the outcome law of the assigned energy observable $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ in the pure preparation of $f$ is purely atomic with
$$\mu^{H_1}_f\bigl(\{E_n\}\bigr)=|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}\quad(n\in\mathbb N),\qquad \mu^{H_1}_f(B)=\sum_{n:\,E_n\in B}|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}$$

(d) **Three-dimensional isotropic realization.** The energy observable $(H_3,\mathrm J)$ of the model definition clause (d) has spectrum $\sigma(H_3)=\{\hbar\omega(M+\tfrac32):M\in\mathbb N\}$; for every $M\in\mathbb N$ the eigenspace $\ker(H_3-\hbar\omega(M+\frac32)I)$ has the orthonormal basis $\{\psi_N:N\in\mathbb N^{3},\ n_1+n_2+n_3=M\}$ and dimension $(M+1)(M+2)/2$; the ground energy is $\tfrac32\hbar\omega$;

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P4, P5, the adopted oscillator model and the cited mathematics. They concern the eigenvalue list, the eigenbasis, the excitation operators and the atomic outcome law of the model's assigned energy observable; they assert no measured spectral line, no numerical value of $m$, $\omega$ or $\hbar$, no apparatus realization, no selection rule and no transition rate. The identification of a laboratory resonance or spectral line with an eigenvalue difference of this model is a tested identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not a consequence of this theorem.

For real $x,y$, $\exp(x+iy)=e^x(\cos y+i\sin y)$ and $|\exp(x+iy)|=e^x$. In particular $e^{i\pi}+1=0$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]], [[thm-eulers-formula]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]], [[thm-pythagorean-and-parity-identities-for-all-six-trigonometric-functions]], [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]], [[def-pi-via-first-positive-cosine-zero]].

The functions $\sin,\cos,\sinh,\cosh$ are entire and satisfy
$$\sin'=\cos,\qquad \cos'=-\sin,\qquad \sinh'=\cosh,\qquad \cosh'=\sinh.$$

For every real $x$, $\sin ^2x+\cos ^2x=1$, $\sin(-x)=-\sin x$, and $\cos(-x)=\cos x$. Wherever the displayed quotients are defined, $\tan(-x)=-\tan x$, $\cot(-x)=-\cot x$, $\sec(-x)=\sec x$, $\csc(-x)=-\csc x$, $1+\tan^2x=\sec^2x$, and $1+\cot^2x=\csc^2x$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]], [[def-tangent-cotangent-secant-cosecant]].

Adopt the postulates P1 and P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable with outcome law $\mu^{A}$ in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and let $\rho$ be a preparation. Then:

(a) **Pure preparations.** Let $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ be the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$. Then the mean of the outcome law exists and equals $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, and the second moment exists and equals $\|A\psi\|^{2}$:
$$m(\psi)=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2},$$
both read in the powers of the declared unit $u_A$ of the observable. If $\psi\in D(A^{2})$, the variance is
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\psi)\bigr)^{2}d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}.$$

(b) **Variance and its hypotheses.** For every unit $\psi\in D(A)$ the variance exists and equals
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\psi}(A)=\|A\psi\|^{2}-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}=\bigl\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\bigr\|^{2}\ge0,$$
without any hypothesis beyond $\psi\in D(A)$; no appeal to a discrete eigenbasis is made.

(c) **Non-existence is possible.** The identities of (a) and (b) are conditional on membership of $\psi$ in the stated domains. If $\psi\notin D(|A|^{1/2})$ then $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\infty$, so the mean of the outcome law does not exist as a finite real number; the mean is finite exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then $\psi$ need not lie in $D(A)$. If $\psi\notin D(A)$ then the second moment $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ is infinite. In particular every preparation of the model is a unit ray or a density operator, and no preparation is equipped with finite moments automatically.

(d) **Mixtures.** Let $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ be a spectral expansion of a preparation, $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, $(u_n)$ orthonormal. In every weighted moment sum, zero-weight terms are defined to be zero before evaluating a component integral; equivalently, only positive-weight indices are summed. This applies also to component means that are undefined at zero-weight indices. Then the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite if and only if $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$, and then $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int\lambda\,dE_{A,u_n}$. For the second moment, put $M_n:=\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,u_n}$, so $M_n=\|Au_n\|^{2}$ for $u_n\in D(A)$ and $M_n=+\infty$ otherwise; a zero weight contributes zero. Then $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_nM_n\in[0,\infty]$, and it is finite exactly when every $u_n$ of positive weight lies in $D(A)$ and $\sum_{n:w_n>0}w_n\|Au_n\|^{2}<\infty$. Thus componentwise domain membership alone does not guarantee a finite mixed-state second moment. Whenever the mixture has a finite absolute first moment, the identity of clause (b) of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] gives its mean as the absolutely convergent weighted average of the component means.

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1 and P2 together with the mathematical moment results cited below; they assert no apparatus resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance and no empirical value. Whether a concrete preparation has a finite mean or variance for a concrete assigned observable is a question about the pair $(\rho,A)$ and the tested identification of the observable, not a consequence of the framework's postulates alone.

**(a) Setting.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the
observable and probability postulate P2 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned sharp observable with
declared unit $u_{A}$ and outcome law $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ in a preparation
$\rho$, in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b).

**(b) Preparation variance.** When the mean
$m(\rho):=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and the second
moment $\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ of the outcome
law are finite, the **preparation variance** of $(A,u_{A})$ in $\rho$ is
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(A):=\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\rho)\bigr)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda),$$
read in the square $u_{A}^{2}$ of the declared unit, and the **preparation
spread** is $\Delta_{\rho}A:=\operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(A)^{1/2}\ge0$, read in
the unit $u_{A}$. When either quantity is not finite the variance and the
spread of the pair in $\rho$ are **not defined**; the definition does not
extend them by $+\infty$.

**(c) Values and hypotheses.** The variance and its hypotheses are exactly
those of the moment theorem: for a pure preparation of a unit vector
$\psi\in D(A)$ the spread is $\Delta_{\psi}A=\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\|$,
equal to $\bigl(\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}\bigr)^{1/2}$
when $\psi\in D(A^{2})$; for a preparation $\rho$ the identities and existence
criteria are those of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] and
[[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]]. In particular a mean exists
exactly when $\rho$ is concentrated on the domain of $|A|^{1/2}$ in the sense
of those items, and no preparation is equipped with finite moments
automatically.

**(d) Products of spreads.** For two assigned sharp observables $(A,u_{A})$
and $(B,u_{B})$ in a common preparation $\rho$ in which both spreads are
defined, the product $\Delta_{\rho}A\,\Delta_{\rho}B$ is a nonnegative real
number read in the product unit $u_{A}u_{B}$; for a pure preparation of a unit
vector in $D(A)\cap D(B)$ it is
$\|(A-a)\psi\|\,\|(B-b)\psi\|$ with the real means $a=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$
and $b=\langle B\psi,\psi\rangle$.

**(e) Reading and scope.** The spread $\Delta_{\rho}A$ is a property of the
pair (preparation, assigned observable): it is the standard deviation of the
outcome law that P2 assigns. It is not an apparatus resolution, not a
measurement error and not a disturbance of the preparation; those are further
objects that require a declared instrument or apparatus model and are not
introduced here. Clause (b) makes no claim that a preparation realizes a
specific laboratory state, that a laboratory procedure measures $A$ with
resolution $u_{A}$, or that the spread is observed in any experiment; the
identification of an apparatus with the pair $(A,u_{A})$ is a tested
identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7.
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] fixes the units in which the
displays are read.

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (a), (b), (c), and the coherent-state family of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-states]]; assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $Q$ and $P$ be the model's position and momentum observables with their declared units ($\mathrm m$ and $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$), let $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, let $\Delta_{\rho}A$ be the preparation spread of an assigned sharp observable in the reading of [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]], and write $\langle A\rangle_z:=\langle A\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle$ for the model's coherent preparation of label $z$. Then:

(a) **Coherent spreads.** For every $z\in\mathbb C$ the vector $\Psi_z$ lies in $D(Q)\cap D(P)$, the preparation spreads of $Q$ and $P$ in the pure preparation of $\Psi_z$ exist, and
$$\Delta_{\Psi_z}Q=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\frac{\hbar}{\ell\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_z}Q\,\Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\frac{\hbar}{2};$$

(b) **Position-momentum relation of the model.** Every unit vector $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$ satisfies
$$\Delta_{f}Q\,\Delta_{f}P\ge\frac{\hbar}{2},$$
read in the product unit $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{2}\mathrm s^{-1}$; consequently the value $\hbar/2$ attained in (a) is the minimum over the common domain, and it is attained by every coherent preparation;

(c) **Saturation.** For every $z\in\mathbb C$, with the centered vectors
$$x_z:=(Q-\langle Q\rangle_zI)\Psi_z,\qquad y_z:=(P-\langle P\rangle_zI)\Psi_z,$$
one has $\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=-i\hbar/2$; in particular $\operatorname{Re}\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=0$ and $x_z,y_z$ are linearly dependent, so $\|x_z\|\,\|y_z\|=|\langle x_z,y_z\rangle|=\hbar/2$;

(d) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P5, the adopted oscillator model, the cited preparation-moment and uncertainty results and the cited mathematics. They concern the spreads of the two separately assigned outcome laws of $Q$ and $P$ in one preparation; they introduce no joint outcome law of position and momentum, no measurement error, no disturbance of the preparation, no dynamics and no empirical value. Whether a laboratory preparation and apparatus realize the pair of observables and produce this spread is a tested identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7.

Let $\iota_{\mathbb R}\colon\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$ be the canonical-natural map
of [[def-canonical-natural]], and let $j\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ be the real
embedding $j(x)=x+i0$ from [[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]. For every
$n\in\mathbb N$, the factorial $n!$ is nonzero by
[[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]], so
$\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!)>0$ by [[lem-of-naturals-positive]] and consequently
$j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))\ne0$ in the complex field
[[thm-complex-numbers-form-a-field]].

For $z\in\mathbb C$, define
$$ \exp z:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^n}{j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))}. $$
whenever this complex series converges. Inside a complex expression we
abbreviate the embedded denominator $j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))$ by $n!$, so the
same definition may be written $\exp z=\sum z^n/n!$ without identifying a
natural number with a complex number. Powers and series are those of
[[def-complex-integer-powers]] and
[[def-complex-series-power-series-and-absolute-convergence]]. The convergence
for every $z\in\mathbb C$ is discharged by
[[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]].
For every $z\in\mathbb C$, the series $\sum z^n/n!$ converges absolutely.

derivations.claim: [The flow and its coherent action] By [F1] the model's flow is the strongly continuous unitary group generated by $-\frac{i}{\hbar}H_1$; by [F2] the explicit spectral family $U(t)f=\sum_ne^{-i\omega(n+\frac12)t}\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\psi_n$ has the same generator, so by the uniqueness of the generator recorded in the autonomous-dynamics reading the two families agree, and $U(t)\Psi_z=e^{-i\omega t/2}\Psi_{z(t)}$ for every $z$ and $t$.

[Energy law of the coherent preparation] By [F3] the coefficients of $\Psi_z$ in the eigenbasis are $\langle\Psi_z,\psi_n\rangle=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}$, so $|\langle\Psi_z,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}$ and the energy law is the atomic law $\mu^{H_1}_{\Psi_z}(\{E_n\})=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}$ with $E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)$; and the mean energy is $\langle H_1\rangle_z=\hbar\omega(|z|^{2}+\frac12)$ by [F3].

[Euler and trigonometric calculus] By [F4], $e^{-i\omega t}=\cos\omega t-i\sin\omega t$, so for $z=z_1+iz_2$ one has $z(t)=z(\cos\omega t-i\sin\omega t)=(z_1\cos\omega t+z_2\sin\omega t)+i(z_2\cos\omega t-z_1\sin\omega t)$, and the derivatives of $\sin$ and $\cos$ are $\cos$ and $-\sin$.

[Clause (a)] By step 1.1, $U(t)\Psi_z=e^{-i\omega t/2}\Psi_{z(t)}$ for every $t$; since $U(t)$ is a bijective linear isometry by [F1], the Schroedinger-picture state of the preparation $[\Psi_z]$ at time $t$ is the ray $[U(t)\Psi_z]=[\Psi_{z(t)}]$, which is again a coherent preparation; the label $z(t)=ze^{-i\omega t}$ rotates with angular frequency $\omega$.

[Clause (b), complex form] By step 1.1 the evolved vector is $e^{-i\omega t/2}\Psi_{z(t)}$, and multiplying by the phase $e^{-i\omega t/2}$ does not change the quadratic-form means; by [F2] and [F5], $\langle Q\rangle_{z(t)}=\sqrt2\ell\operatorname{Re}z(t)$ and $\langle P\rangle_{z(t)}=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z(t)$.

[Clause (c)] By step 1.1 the preparation at time $t$ is the coherent preparation of label $z(t)$, so [F6] applied with $w=z(t)$ gives $\Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}Q=\ell/\sqrt2$, $\Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}P=\hbar/(\ell\sqrt2)$ and product $\hbar/2$ for every $t$: the spreads are constant along the evolution.

[Clause (d), Poisson law and energy spread] Let $p_n:=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}$ and $s:=|z|^{2}$. By step 1.2 the law is $\mu^{H_1}_{\Psi_z}(\{E_n\})=p_n$; by [F7], $\sum_np_n=e^{-s}\sum_n\frac{s^{n}}{n!}=1$, $\sum_nnp_n=e^{-s}\sum_nn\frac{s^{n}}{n!}=e^{-s}se^{s}=s$, and $\sum_nn^{2}p_n=e^{-s}\sum_nn^{2}\frac{s^{n}}{n!}=e^{-s}\bigl(s^{2}e^{s}+se^{s}\bigr)=s^{2}+s$, because $n^{2}=n(n-1)+n$ and the two reindexed series of [F7] apply. Hence the number-coordinate variance is $\sum_n(n-s)^{2}p_n=(s^{2}+s)-s^{2}=s=|z|^{2}$. Since $E_n-\hbar\omega(s+\frac12)=\hbar\omega(n-s)$, the energy-law variance is $(\hbar\omega)^2s$, and by the outcome-law spread definition [F5] its square root is $\Delta_{\Psi_z}H_1=\hbar\omega|z|$. Thus the energy law is the affine image of the Poisson law of parameter $|z|^{2}$ under $n\mapsto E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)$; at $s=0$ the convention $s^0=1$ gives $p_0=1$ and $p_n=0$ for $n\ge1$.

[Clause (b), classical form] By step 2.2 and step 1.3, with $z=z_1+iz_2$, $x(t)=\sqrt2\ell(z_1\cos\omega t+z_2\sin\omega t)$ and $p(t)=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar}{\ell}(z_2\cos\omega t-z_1\sin\omega t)$; since $x_0=\sqrt2\ell z_1$ and $\frac{p_0}{m\omega}=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar z_2}{\ell m\omega}=\sqrt2\ell z_2$ by $\ell^{2}=\hbar/(m\omega)$, while $m\omega x_0=\sqrt2\,m\omega\ell z_1=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar z_1}{\ell}$ by the same identity, the displays $x(t)=x_0\cos\omega t+\frac{p_0}{m\omega}\sin\omega t$ and $p(t)=p_0\cos\omega t-m\omega x_0\sin\omega t$ follow. Differentiating with the trigonometric derivatives of step 1.3 gives $\dot x(t)=-x_0\omega\sin\omega t+\frac{p_0}{m}\cos\omega t=\frac{p(t)}{m}$ and $\dot p(t)=-p_0\omega\sin\omega t-m\omega x_0\omega\cos\omega t=-m\omega^{2}\bigl(x_0\cos\omega t+\frac{p_0}{m\omega}\sin\omega t\bigr)=-m\omega^{2}x(t)$ for every $t$.

[Clause (e)] Clauses (a), (b), (c) and (d) were obtained from the model's flow and energy observable, the explicit coherent evolution, the coherent fluctuation theorem and the exponential and trigonometric identities; no measurement record, apparatus model, damping or driving and no empirical value entered, and the identification of the mean motion with a laboratory oscillator is a tested identification under P7. This is clause (e).

boundaries.evidence: Step 2.4 defines the Poisson weights $p_n=e^{-|z|^{2}}|z|^{2n}/n!$ with $\sum_np_n=1$; an empty set of outcome indices receives mass $0$ by countable additivity of the law, as in step 2.4's computation of the atomic masses.

Statement defines x0=p0=0 at z=0. Step 2.4 adopts s^0=1 at s=0, gives p0=1 and pn=0 for n>=1, mean energy hbar omega/2 and zero energy spread. Means are stationary at zero while Q/P spreads remain nonzero.
The flow is applied to one member $\Psi_z$ of the family at a time; step 2.1 covers a single $t$, so the one-parameter case is the statement.
Step 2.4 covers the degenerate amplitude $|z|=0$ where $\Delta H_1=\hbar\omega|z|=0$ and the Poisson law collapses to $\delta_0$ shifted by $\hbar\omega/2$; step 3.1 remains valid with $x_0=p_0=0$.

Step 2.2 verifies the values at $t=0$ and at the quarter period $t=\pi/(2\omega)$; step 3.1 restores the closed forms at these endpoints, and step 2.1 records the global phase $-1$ at the period endpoint $t=2\pi/\omega$.

The Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice are assumed in the statement and used only through the spectral and flow suppliers of [F1], [F2] and [F7]; steps 1.1-3.1 invoke no further choice.

boundaries.reason: Clauses (a)-(d) assert the evolved preparation, the mean motion, the stationary spreads and the Poisson law; no biconditional is asserted.
No converse implication is asserted; in particular the statement does not claim that every preparation with periodic mean motion is coherent, and step 4.1 records this scope limit.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix real parameters $m>0$, $\omega>0$, $\hbar>0$, put $\ell:=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}>0$, and let $g_0,P,(g_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be the Hermite data of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-recurrence]] in $L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$, so that $(g_n)$ is a complete orthonormal family by [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-completeness]]. Define

$$D:L^2(\mathbb R,dy)\to L^2(\mathbb R,dx),\qquad (Df)(x):=\ell^{-1/2}f(x/\ell),$$

and let $A$ be the self-adjoint diagonal operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]] for the complete orthonormal family $(g_n)$ and the eigenvalues $\lambda_n=2n+1$, with the core $P$ and spectrum $\{2n+1:n\in\mathbb N\}$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-spectrum]]).

Then:

(a) $D$ is a linear isometry of $L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$ onto $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$ with two-sided inverse $(D^{-1}g)(y)=\ell^{1/2}g(\ell y)$; the functions $\psi_n:=Dg_n$, $\psi_n(x)=\ell^{-1/2}g_n(x/\ell)$, form a complete orthonormal family of $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$;

(b) the operator

$$H_{\mathrm{osc}}:=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\,DAD^{-1},\qquad D(H_{\mathrm{osc}}):=\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R,dx):D^{-1}f\in D(A)\},$$

is self-adjoint, satisfies $H_{\mathrm{osc}}\psi_n=\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)\psi_n$ for every $n$, and has

$$D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})=\Bigl\{f:\sum_n\hbar^2\omega^2(n+\tfrac12)^2|c_n|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad H_{\mathrm{osc}}f=\sum_n\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)c_n\psi_n,$$

where $c_n:=\langle D^{-1}f,g_n\rangle=\langle f,\psi_n\rangle$; its spectrum is $\sigma(H_{\mathrm{osc}})=\{\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12):n\in\mathbb N\}$, its ground energy is $\hbar\omega/2$ with eigenvector $\psi_0$, and $\langle H_{\mathrm{osc}}f,f\rangle\ge\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\|f\|^2$ for every $f\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$;

(c) $D(P)=\operatorname{span}\{\psi_n\}$ is a core for $H_{\mathrm{osc}}$, and for every polynomial $p$ the function $f:=D(pg_0)$ is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R$ with

$$H_{\mathrm{osc}}f=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}f''+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2f$$

pointwise on $\mathbb R$;

(d) for every $f\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ and every test function $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$,

$$\int_{\mathbb R}(H_{\mathrm{osc}}f)(x)\varphi(x)\,dx=\int_{\mathbb R}f(x)\Bigl(-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\varphi''(x)+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2\varphi(x)\Bigr)dx,$$

so $H_{\mathrm{osc}}$ is the self-adjoint realization of the differential expression $-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\frac{d^2}{dx^2}+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2$ in the weak sense; no identification of $D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ with a separately defined maximal differential-operator domain is asserted.

All parameters enter as positive real numbers; no physical identification of $m,\omega,\hbar$ with measured quantities is made.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $L^2=L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$ be the complex Lebesgue space with inner product $\langle\varphi,\psi\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R}\varphi(y)\overline{\psi(y)}\,dy$ linear in the first argument ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]], [[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]); this pairing makes $L^2$ a complex Hilbert space by [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]. For complex-valued functions, smoothness and derivatives use the componentwise convention of [[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]. Write $g_0$ for the function $g_0(y):=\pi^{-1/4}e^{-y^{2}/2}$ and also for its class in $L^2$. Put

$$P:=\{p\,g_0:\ p\in\mathbb C[y]\}\subseteq L^2 ,$$

the set of classes of polynomial multiples of $g_0$. Each class in $P$ has a unique representative of the form $p g_0$: if $p g_0=qg_0$ almost everywhere, the continuous function $(p-q)g_0$ vanishes almost everywhere and therefore everywhere, and $g_0(y)>0$ for every $y$, so $p=q$. Let $Y$ be multiplication by $y$ and $\partial_y$ the derivative, acting on this unique smooth representative. Set $g_{-1}:=0$ for use in the recurrence formulas at $n=0$. Define

$$a:=\frac{Y+\partial_y}{\sqrt2},\qquad a^\dagger:=\frac{Y-\partial_y}{\sqrt2},\qquad g_n:=\frac{(a^\dagger)^ng_0}{\sqrt{n!}}\quad(n\in\mathbb N).$$

Then:

(a) $g_0\in L^2$ with $\|g_0\|=1$; more generally $y^kg_0\in L^2$ for every $k\in\mathbb N$, so $P$ is a linear subspace of $L^2$ all of whose members are represented by $C^\infty$ functions;

(b) $Y,\partial_y,a,a^\dagger$ map $P$ into $P$, and $\partial_y(pg_0)=(p'-yp)g_0$ for every polynomial $p$;

(c) for all $\varphi,\psi\in P$, $\langle a^\dagger\varphi,\psi\rangle=\langle\varphi,a\psi\rangle$ and $\langle a\varphi,\psi\rangle=\langle\varphi,a^\dagger\psi\rangle$;

(d) $a^\dagger a-a a^\dagger=-I$ on $P$, i.e. $[a,a^\dagger]=aa^\dagger-a^\dagger a=I$ on $P$, and $ag_0=0$;

(e) for every $n\in\mathbb N$: $ag_n=\sqrt n\,g_{n-1}$ (with $ag_0=0$), $a^\dagger g_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,g_{n+1}$, $a^\dagger ag_n=ng_n$ and $aa^\dagger g_n=(n+1)g_n$;

(f) the polynomials

$$H_n(y):=(-1)^ne^{y^2}\frac{d^n}{dy^n}e^{-y^2}$$

are polynomials of degree $n$ with leading coefficient $2^n$, $H_0=1$, $H_1(y)=2y$, $H_n(-y)=(-1)^nH_n(y)$, and they satisfy

$$H_n'=2nH_{n-1},\qquad H_{n+1}=2yH_n-2nH_{n-1}\qquad(n\ge1);$$

moreover

$$g_n=\frac{H_ng_0}{\sqrt{2^nn!}};$$

(g) consequently

$$\sqrt2\,y\,g_n=\sqrt n\,g_{n-1}+\sqrt{n+1}\,g_{n+1},\qquad \sqrt2\,g_n'=\sqrt n\,g_{n-1}-\sqrt{n+1}\,g_{n+1}.$$

**(a) Setting.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 in the reading of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]) and the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (a), (b), (c), with parameters $m>0$, $\omega>0$, action constant $\hbar>0$ and length scale $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(g_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be the Hermite family of $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$, let $D:L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)\to L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$ be the scaling unitary and $(\psi_n)$ the scaled eigenbasis of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (a), (b), with $\psi_n=Dg_n$; let $a_\psi=DaD^{-1}$ be the transported annihilation operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]], and let $N_\psi=DND^{-1}$ be the model's assigned excitation-number observable of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clause (c), with its stated domain and unit $1/\mathrm{count}$.

**(b) The family.** For $z\in\mathbb C$ let $\psi^{(y)}_z$ be the coherent vector of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-convergence]] clause (a),
$$\psi^{(y)}_z:=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}\,g_n\in L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy),$$
the series converging in $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$, and define the model's **coherent state** with label $z$ by
$$\Psi_z:=D\psi^{(y)}_z=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}\,\psi_n\in\mathcal H_1 .$$
The family $(\Psi_z)_{z\in\mathbb C}$ is the model's **coherent-state family**, and $z$ is its **amplitude-phase label**.

**(c) Basic properties.** The following properties of the family are those established in the cited items and are recorded here as part of the definition's reading: the series for $\Psi_z$ converges and $\|\Psi_z\|=1$, so by P1 the ray $[\Psi_z]$ is a pure preparation of the model when it is declared as one; $\Psi_z\in D(N_\psi^{k})$ for every $k\in\mathbb N$; $a_\psi\Psi_z=z\Psi_z$, so $\Psi_z$ is a unit eigenvector of the annihilation operator with eigenvalue $z$; $\langle\Psi_z,\Psi_w\rangle=e^{-(|z|^{2}+|w|^{2})/2+z\overline w}$, with modulus $e^{-|z-w|^{2}/2}$ for all $z,w$, so distinct labels define distinct preparations (their overlap modulus is less than $1$, whereas unit vectors on the same ray have overlap modulus $1$) and no two members of the family are orthogonal; and $\Psi_0=\psi_0$ is the ground eigenvector of the energy operator. ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-convergence]] clauses (a), (b), (c), (d), (e), transported by the unitary $D$ of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clause (a).)

**(d) Reading of the label.** The label $z$ is dimensionless (it is a complex number, not a quantity with a physical dimension). Its amplitude is $|z|$; when $z\ne0$, its phase is the class $\arg z\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, while $z=0$ has zero amplitude and no phase label. The mathematical coherent-state series gives the quadratic-form value $\langle N_\psi\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=|z|^{2}$ for the assigned, dimensionless excitation-number observable $(N_\psi,1/\mathrm{count})$; this is the number coordinate intended by the model's P2 reading. The coherent-state evolution result shows that the preparation means of position and momentum rotate with the phase label at angular frequency $\omega$. Clause (d) records this interpretation of the label, not an outcome of measuring the label itself.

**(e) Scope.** The definition declares a one-parameter family of preparations of the one-dimensional model and fixes its notation. It does not assert that the coherent states are the only preparations with time-independent position or momentum spreads, it does not assert minimality of any uncertainty product (that is a separate result for this family), it does not construct a displacement operator, an overcompleteness relation or a resolution of unity, and it makes no measurement, apparatus or empirical claim. The two presentations of the family -- as eigenvectors of the annihilation operator, as in clause (b), and as translated ground states -- are not identified here; only the former is defined.

Let $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, let $(g_n)$, $D$, $A$, $(\psi_n)$ and $H_1$ be the Hermite family, the unitary, the dimensionless diagonal operator, the scaled eigenbasis and the energy operator of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (a) and (b), so that $\psi_n=Dg_n$ and $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ is the model's one-dimensional assigned energy observable of the model definition clause (c). Put
$$N_\psi:=DND^{-1},\qquad a_\psi:=DaD^{-1},\qquad a^\dagger_\psi:=Da^\dagger D^{-1},$$
where $N$ is the number operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]] and $N_\psi$ is the assigned excitation-number observable with unit $1/\mathrm{count}$ of the model definition clause (c); these are the number and ladder operators transported from that lemma, with domains $D(N_\psi)=\{Dx:x\in D(N)\}$, $D(a_\psi)=\{Dx:x\in D(a)\}$ and $D(a^\dagger_\psi)=\{Dx:x\in D(a^\dagger)\}$. Write $E_n:=\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)$ and, for the three-dimensional realization of the model definition clause (d), let $(H_3,\mathrm J)$ and $(\psi_N)_{N\in\mathbb N^3}$ be its assigned energy observable and its product eigenbasis.
