(a) **Spectrum, eigenbasis and simplicity.** $D(H_1)=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:\sum_nn^{2}|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}<\infty\}$, the family $(\psi_n)$ is a complete orthonormal family of $\mathcal H_1$ and a core for $H_1$, $H_1\psi_n=E_n\psi_n$, and the spectrum and eigenspaces are
$$\sigma(H_1)=\{E_n:n\in\mathbb N\},\qquad \ker(H_1-E_nI)=\mathbb C\psi_n\quad(n\in\mathbb N);$$
the ground energy is $E_0=\hbar\omega/2$ and the gap between consecutive levels is $E_{n+1}-E_n=\hbar\omega$;

(b) **Excitation reading.** $H_1=\hbar\omega\bigl(N_\psi+\tfrac12I\bigr)$ with common domain $D(H_1)=D(N_\psi)$; $N_\psi$ is self-adjoint with spectrum $\mathbb N$ and eigenbasis $(\psi_n)$; $a_\psi$ and $a^\dagger_\psi$ are closed with $a_\psi^{*}=a^\dagger_\psi$, and on the eigenbasis
$$a_\psi\psi_n=\sqrt n\,\psi_{n-1}\ (n\ge1),\qquad a_\psi\psi_0=0,\qquad a^\dagger_\psi\psi_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,\psi_{n+1},\qquad N_\psi\psi_n=n\psi_n;$$
the eigenspace of $N_\psi$ at each $n\in\mathbb N$ is exactly $\mathbb C\psi_n$, so its nonzero eigenvectors are precisely the nonzero scalar multiples of the $\psi_n$; the outcome law of $N_\psi$ in the pure preparation of $\psi_n$ is the point mass $\delta_n$;

(c) **Energy outcome law.** For every unit $f\in\mathcal H_1$ the outcome law of the assigned energy observable $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ in the pure preparation of $f$ is purely atomic with
$$\mu^{H_1}_f\bigl(\{E_n\}\bigr)=|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}\quad(n\in\mathbb N),\qquad \mu^{H_1}_f(B)=\sum_{n:\,E_n\in B}|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}$$
for every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$, and $\mu^{H_1}_f(\sigma(H_1))=1$; in particular the law has no mass outside $\{E_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$, and $E_n$ is an atom of the law of $f$ exactly when $\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\ne0$;

(d) **Three-dimensional isotropic realization.** The energy observable $(H_3,\mathrm J)$ of the model definition clause (d) has spectrum $\sigma(H_3)=\{\hbar\omega(M+\tfrac32):M\in\mathbb N\}$; for every $M\in\mathbb N$ the eigenspace $\ker(H_3-\hbar\omega(M+\frac32)I)$ has the orthonormal basis $\{\psi_N:N\in\mathbb N^{3},\ n_1+n_2+n_3=M\}$ and dimension $(M+1)(M+2)/2$; the ground energy is $\tfrac32\hbar\omega$;

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P4, P5, the adopted oscillator model and the cited mathematics. They concern the eigenvalue list, the eigenbasis, the excitation operators and the atomic outcome law of the model's assigned energy observable; they assert no measured spectral line, no numerical value of $m$, $\omega$ or $\hbar$, no apparatus realization, no selection rule and no transition rate. The identification of a laboratory resonance or spectral line with an eigenvalue difference of this model is a tested identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not a consequence of this theorem.

**(a) Adopted framework assumptions.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, in the readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]], [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix real model parameters $m>0$ (mass parameter, unit $\mathrm{kg}$), $\omega>0$ (angular frequency, unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$) and the action constant $\hbar>0$ (unit $\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$) of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)4, and put
$$\ell:=\sqrt{\frac{\hbar}{m\omega}}>0\qquad\text{(unit }\mathrm m\text{),}$$
the model's length scale.

**(b) One-dimensional realization.** Write $\mathcal H_1:=L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx;\mathbb C)$ for the model's one-dimensional state space, the complex Hilbert space of almost-everywhere classes with inner product linear in the first argument, taken in the scalar reading $r=1$ of the component-valued space of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] for $d=1$. The model's **position** and **momentum** are the operators of that lemma at $d=1$, $r=1$, namely
$$Q:=M_x,\qquad D(Q)=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:xf\in L^{2}\},\qquad (Qf)(x)=xf(x),$$
$$P:=-i\hbar D_x,\qquad D(P)=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:\text{the weak derivative }D_xf\text{ lies in }L^{2}\},\qquad Pf=-i\hbar D_xf,$$
which are densely defined and self-adjoint with exactly these domains; the model assigns to $(Q,\mathrm m)$ and to $(P,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$ the status of assigned sharp observables in the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), with outcome laws read from P2.

**(c) Energy and excitation-number observables.** Let $g_0,(g_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ and the unitary $D:L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)\to L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$ be the Hermite data and scaling map of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (a), (b) for the parameters $m,\omega,\hbar$. Put $\mathscr P_y:=\{p g_0:p\in\mathbb C[y]\}\subseteq L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$; the Hermite recurrence [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-recurrence]] identifies this polynomial-Gaussian space with $\operatorname{span}\{g_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$, and its scaled image $\mathscr P_x:=D(\mathscr P_y)=\operatorname{span}\{\psi_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$ is the core supplied by the scaling theorem. Let $A$ be the diagonal operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]] for the family $(g_n)$ and eigenvalues $2n+1$. The model's **energy operator** is
$$H_1:=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\,D A D^{-1},\qquad D(H_1):=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:D^{-1}f\in D(A)\},$$
the operator of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clause (b); its exact domain, action, spectrum and eigenbasis are those established there. The model assigns to $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ the status of assigned energy observable of the isolated system in the sense of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clauses (a) and (b): the model's flow is $U(t)=\exp(-itH_1/\hbar)$ and the model's Schroedinger dynamics is the one of that definition. Let $N$ be the self-adjoint number operator on $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$ of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]] for the Hermite family $(g_n)$, and set $N_\psi:=DND^{-1}$. Its transported domain and action are
$$D(N_\psi)=\Bigl\{f\in\mathcal H_1:\sum_n n^2|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad N_\psi f=\sum_n n\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\psi_n,$$
with the series converging in $\mathcal H_1$; it is self-adjoint by [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-unitary-transport-of-spectral-pvms]] clauses (a), (d). The model assigns to $(N_\psi,1/\mathrm{count})$ the status of its dimensionless excitation-number observable; here $\mathrm{count}$ denotes one excitation count and is dimensionless, so the spectral coordinate $n$ records $n$ excitations, and its outcome laws are read by P2. On the scaled polynomial-Gaussian core $\mathscr P_x$ the operator $H_1$ is the self-adjoint realization of the quadratic expression: for every $f\in\mathscr P_x$,
$$H_1f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}f''+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}f$$
pointwise, and for every $f\in D(H_1)$ the weak identity $\int (H_1f)\varphi\,dx=\int f\bigl(-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\varphi''+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}\varphi\bigr)dx$ holds for every $\varphi\in C_c^{\infty}(\mathbb R)$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (c), (d)). The formal differential expression $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\frac{d^{2}}{dx^{2}}+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}$ is the model's **quadratic potential energy plus kinetic energy** reading; no identification of $D(H_1)$ with any independently defined maximal differential-operator domain, and no separate quadratic-form-domain characterization, is asserted.

**(d) Three-dimensional isotropic realization.** For the spinless reading $s=0$ of the massive-particle model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]], with state space $\mathcal H_3:=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dx;\mathbb C)$, position operators $Q_j$ and momentum operators $P_k$ ($j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$) with the domains and units of that definition, the model with common frequency $\omega$ has **energy operator** $H_3$ equal to the diagonal operator $H$ of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-multidimensional-oscillator-completeness]] clause (c) for $d=3$, $m_j=m$, $\omega_j=\omega$, a self-adjoint operator on $\mathcal H_3$ with the domain, spectrum and core displayed there. The model assigns to $(H_3,\mathrm J)$ the status of assigned energy observable in the reading of clause (c); its eigenbasis and the identity $H_3=\sum_{j=1}^{3}\bigl(-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\partial_{x_j}^{2}+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x_j^{2}\bigr)$ on the core are those of that theorem, and the one-dimensional realization of clauses (b) and (c) is the coordinate specialization of this one.

**(e) Physical reading and scope.** Clause (c) defines the model quantities that the page calls the energy and excitation number; it is a **model assumption** that the energy of the declared isolated particle is the assigned observable $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ and that $(N_\psi,1/\mathrm{count})$ is its excitation-number observable. The additive constant of the potential energy is removed at the minimum: for a one-dimensional potential-energy function $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^2$, with values in joules for position $x$ in metres, suppose $V$ has a non-degenerate local minimum at $0$, meaning $V'(0)=0$ and $V''(0)>0$. Taylor's theorem gives $V(x)-V(0)=\frac{1}{2}V''(0)x^{2}+o(x^{2})$ as $x\to0$; the oscillator model approximates this shifted potential-energy function by its quadratic term and sets $m\omega^{2}=V''(0)$. The oscillator's quantum ground energy in this convention is $\hbar\omega/2$. With only the stated $C^2$ regularity, the remainder is $o(x^2)$; no quantitative finite-amplitude error bound is asserted on this page (Binney §3.1, cited in the references). No measured value, no laboratory identification and no derivation of $m$ or $\omega$ from any microscopic or environmental theory is asserted. The model contains no damping, no external driving, no time-dependent parameters, no coupling to electromagnetic fields or radiation, no spin-dependent force, no anharmonic term, no relativistic correction and no boundary or many-body effect; those are separate model assumptions belonging to their own items. The parameters $m$ and $\omega$ are model parameters of dimensions $\mu$ and $\tau^{-1}$ in the conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and all displayed quantities are read in the units fixed there.

**(f) Status.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the objects used by the theorems of this page and record the readings of P1, P2, P4 and P5 in the model's terminology. They assert no preparation or apparatus model, no detection model, no joint outcome law of position and momentum and no empirical result.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space with $\mu(X)>0$, let $m:X\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and finite $\mu$-almost everywhere, and on the complex Hilbert space $H=L^{2}(X,\mu;\mathbb C)$ ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]], [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) let
$$D(M_{m})=\Bigl\{f\in H:\int_{X}|m|^{2}|f|^{2}\,d\mu<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad M_{m}f=mf .$$
Then:

(a) $M_m$ is self-adjoint on $D(M_m)$.

(b) The assignment $E(B):=M_{\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}}$ on Borel sets $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a regular projection-valued measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and for a unit vector $\psi\in H$
$$\|E(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{m^{-1}(B)}|\psi|^{2}\,d\mu .$$

(c) The operator identity $\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE(\lambda)=M_{m}$ holds with domain $D(M_{m})$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]); consequently $E$ is the spectral projection-valued measure of $M_{m}$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]).

(d) $E(B)=0$ if and only if $\mu(m^{-1}(B))=0$, and the spectrum $\sigma(M_{m})$ equals the essential range of $m$:
$$\sigma(M_{m})=\{\,t\in\mathbb R:\mu(m^{-1}(t-\varepsilon,t+\varepsilon))>0\ \text{for every}\ \varepsilon>0\,\}.$$

Let $n\ge1$ and $t>0$. The **heat kernel on $\mathbb R^n$** is the function

$$\Gamma(x,t):=(4\pi t)^{-n/2}\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{|x|^2}{4t}\Bigr),\qquad x\in\mathbb R^n,$$

where $|x|^2=\langle x,x\rangle$ is the Euclidean square of
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and $\exp$ is the real exponential function of
[[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]]. For fixed $t>0$ the map
$x\mapsto\Gamma(x,t)$ is a composite of the quadratic form with the exponential
and a scalar multiple, so it is $C^\infty$ in the sense of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]] by
[[thm-derivative-of-exponential]] and
[[thm-ck-euclidean-maps-closed-under-algebra-and-composition]], and it is
strictly positive by [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]]. The
spatial Laplacian entering the heat equation is that of
[[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]].

The **causal extension** of the heat kernel is $\Gamma(x,t)$ for $t>0$ and
$\Gamma(x,t):=0$ for $t\le0$; the displayed formula is not evaluated at $t=0$
as a function value. The normalisation is fixed by the unit-mass identity
proved for the kernel on this page, and the causal extension is used only as a
locally integrable function or, after embedding, as a distribution.

Assume Countable Choice and let $n\ge1$. For every $t>0$: (i) $\Gamma(\cdot,t)>0$
and $\int_{\mathbb R^n}\Gamma(x,t)\,dx=1$; (ii) parabolic scaling:
$\Gamma(\lambda x,\lambda^2t)=\lambda^{-n}\Gamma(x,t)$ for every $\lambda>0$ and
$x\in\mathbb R^n$; (iii) $\Gamma$ is $C^\infty$ on
$\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)$ and solves the heat equation there,
$\partial_t\Gamma(x,t)=\Delta_x\Gamma(x,t)$; (iv) for every multi-index $\alpha$
there is $C_{n,\alpha}<\infty$ with
$|D^\alpha_x\Gamma(x,t)|\le C_{n,\alpha}t^{-(|\alpha|+n)/2}e^{-|x|^2/(8t)}$ for
all $x\in\mathbb R^n$, $t>0$; in particular $\|\Gamma(\cdot,t)\|_1=1$ and
$(\Gamma(\cdot,t))_{t>0}$ is an $L^1$ approximate identity on $\mathbb R^n$.

Assume Countable Choice. For $n\ge1$ and $t>0$, all first and second moments
are absolutely integrable and
$$\int_{\mathbb R^n}x_i\Gamma(x,t)\,dx=0,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R^n}x_ix_j\Gamma(x,t)\,dx=2t\delta_{ij}.$$
In particular $\int_{\mathbb R^n}|x|^2\Gamma(x,t)\,dx=2nt$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the
cited scalar operator and spectral suppliers. Fix integers $d\ge1$, $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$. Let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the
component-valued space of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]]
with its componentwise inner product, let $Q_{j}^{(1)},P_{k}^{(1)}$ be the
scalar position and momentum operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]], and let
$\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with
$\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^{1}$
([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Write
$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}:=\Psi_{0}\bigl(\bigoplus_{l}\mathcal F_{2}\bigr)\Psi_{0}^{-1}$
for its componentwise version, with $\Psi_{0}$ the unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] clause (a).
Define, componentwise,
$$D(Q_{j}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (Q_{j}f)_{l}:=x_{j}f_{l},$$
$$D(P_{k}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ D_{k}f_{l}\text{ exists in }L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
where $D_{k}$ is the weak derivative of [[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]].
Write $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the classes whose components
lie in $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]),
and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the componentwise Schwartz
class ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]). Then:

(a) under $\Psi_{0}$ the operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are the orthogonal sums
$\bigoplus_{l}Q_{j}^{(1)}$ and $\bigoplus_{l}P_{k}^{(1)}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-orthogonal-sums-of-self-adjoint-operators]]; in particular
$Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are densely defined and self-adjoint with the displayed
domains;

(b) $\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}$ is unitary,
$$D(P_{k})=\bigl\{f\in H^{(r)}:\ \xi_{k}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\bigr\},$$
and for every $f\in D(P_{k})$
$$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}(P_{k}f)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi_{k}\,\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f(\xi)\qquad\text{for almost every }\xi;$$

(c) the componentwise translation $T_{a}^{(r)}f:=f(\cdot-a)$, $a\in\mathbb R^{d}$,
is unitary, leaves $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
invariant, satisfies $D_{k}(T_{a}^{(r)}f)=T_{a}^{(r)}(D_{k}f)$ for
$f\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
$$T_{a}^{(r)}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}Q_{j}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I,\qquad T_{a}^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}P_{k}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=P_{k};$$

(d) for every $f\in D(P_{j})$,
$$\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t\bigl(T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}f-f\bigr)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}f \qquad\text{in }H^{(r)},$$
so the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}$ has generator $-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}$ and
$$T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}=\exp\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tP_{j}\Bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the exponential being the spectral-calculus flow of the self-adjoint operator
$P_{j}$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]]) and let $U:H\to K$ be a bijective linear map with
$$\langle Ux,Uy\rangle_K=\langle x,y\rangle_H\qquad\text{for all }x,y\in H .$$
Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_T$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), and define
$$D(T'):=U D(T),\qquad T'(Ux):=U(Tx)\quad(x\in D(T)).$$
Then:

(a) $T'$ is well defined, linear, densely defined and self-adjoint on $K$;

(b) the assignment $E(B):=U E_T(B) U^{-1}$ on Borel sets $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a regular projection-valued measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, and it is the spectral projection-valued measure of $T'$;

(c) for every unit vector $x\in H$ the scalar laws of the two operators agree,
$$\mu^{T'}_{Ux}(B):=\|E(B)Ux\|_K^2=\|E_T(B)x\|_H^2=:\mu^{T}_x(B)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel});$$

(d) $\sigma(T')=\sigma(T)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space with $\mu(X)>0$, let $m:X\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and finite $\mu$-almost everywhere, and on the complex Hilbert space $H=L^{2}(X,\mu;\mathbb C)$ ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]], [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) let
$$D(M_{m})=\Bigl\{f\in H:\int_{X}|m|^{2}|f|^{2}\,d\mu<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad M_{m}f=mf .$$
Then:

(a) $M_m$ is self-adjoint on $D(M_m)$.

(b) The assignment $E(B):=M_{\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}}$ on Borel sets $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a regular projection-valued measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and for a unit vector $\psi\in H$
$$\|E(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{m^{-1}(B)}|\psi|^{2}\,d\mu .$$

(c) The operator identity $\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE(\lambda)=M_{m}$ holds with domain $D(M_{m})$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]); consequently $E$ is the spectral projection-valued measure of $M_{m}$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]).

(d) $E(B)=0$ if and only if $\mu(m^{-1}(B))=0$, and the spectrum $\sigma(M_{m})$ equals the essential range of $m$:
$$\sigma(M_{m})=\{\,t\in\mathbb R:\mu(m^{-1}(t-\varepsilon,t+\varepsilon))>0\ \text{for every}\ \varepsilon>0\,\}.$$

Assume countable choice. For $n\ge1$, $t>0$, and $\xi\in\mathbb R^n$,
$$\mathcal F(e^{-\pi t|x|^2})(\xi)=t^{-n/2}e^{-\pi|\xi|^2/t}.$$
Every polynomial times a positive real Gaussian is absolutely integrable.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism. If $f : V \to \mathbb C$ belongs to $L^1(\lambda_n)$,
then
$$ \int_V f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y) = \int_U f(T(x))\,|\det DT(x)|\,d\lambda_n(x). $$

Adopt the postulates P1 and P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable with outcome law $\mu^{A}$ in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and let $\rho$ be a preparation. Then:

(a) **Pure preparations.** Let $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ be the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$. Then the mean of the outcome law exists and equals $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, and the second moment exists and equals $\|A\psi\|^{2}$:
$$m(\psi)=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2},$$
both read in the powers of the declared unit $u_A$ of the observable. If $\psi\in D(A^{2})$, the variance is
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\psi)\bigr)^{2}d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}.$$

(b) **Variance and its hypotheses.** For every unit $\psi\in D(A)$ the variance exists and equals
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\psi}(A)=\|A\psi\|^{2}-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}=\bigl\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\bigr\|^{2}\ge0,$$
without any hypothesis beyond $\psi\in D(A)$; no appeal to a discrete eigenbasis is made.

(c) **Non-existence is possible.** The identities of (a) and (b) are conditional on membership of $\psi$ in the stated domains. If $\psi\notin D(|A|^{1/2})$ then $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\infty$, so the mean of the outcome law does not exist as a finite real number; the mean is finite exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then $\psi$ need not lie in $D(A)$. If $\psi\notin D(A)$ then the second moment $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ is infinite. In particular every preparation of the model is a unit ray or a density operator, and no preparation is equipped with finite moments automatically.

(d) **Mixtures.** Let $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ be a spectral expansion of a preparation, $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, $(u_n)$ orthonormal. In every weighted moment sum, zero-weight terms are defined to be zero before evaluating a component integral; equivalently, only positive-weight indices are summed. This applies also to component means that are undefined at zero-weight indices. Then the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite if and only if $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$, and then $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int\lambda\,dE_{A,u_n}$. For the second moment, put $M_n:=\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,u_n}$, so $M_n=\|Au_n\|^{2}$ for $u_n\in D(A)$ and $M_n=+\infty$ otherwise; a zero weight contributes zero. Then $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_nM_n\in[0,\infty]$, and it is finite exactly when every $u_n$ of positive weight lies in $D(A)$ and $\sum_{n:w_n>0}w_n\|Au_n\|^{2}<\infty$. Thus componentwise domain membership alone does not guarantee a finite mixed-state second moment. Whenever the mixture has a finite absolute first moment, the identity of clause (b) of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] gives its mean as the absolutely convergent weighted average of the component means.

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1 and P2 together with the mathematical moment results cited below; they assert no apparatus resolution, no measurement error, no disturbance and no empirical value. Whether a concrete preparation has a finite mean or variance for a concrete assigned observable is a question about the pair $(\rho,A)$ and the tested identification of the observable, not a consequence of the framework's postulates alone.

**(a) Setting.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the
observable and probability postulate P2 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned sharp observable with
declared unit $u_{A}$ and outcome law $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ in a preparation
$\rho$, in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b).

**(b) Preparation variance.** When the mean
$m(\rho):=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and the second
moment $\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ of the outcome
law are finite, the **preparation variance** of $(A,u_{A})$ in $\rho$ is
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(A):=\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\rho)\bigr)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda),$$
read in the square $u_{A}^{2}$ of the declared unit, and the **preparation
spread** is $\Delta_{\rho}A:=\operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(A)^{1/2}\ge0$, read in
the unit $u_{A}$. When either quantity is not finite the variance and the
spread of the pair in $\rho$ are **not defined**; the definition does not
extend them by $+\infty$.

**(c) Values and hypotheses.** The variance and its hypotheses are exactly
those of the moment theorem: for a pure preparation of a unit vector
$\psi\in D(A)$ the spread is $\Delta_{\psi}A=\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\|$,
equal to $\bigl(\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}\bigr)^{1/2}$
when $\psi\in D(A^{2})$; for a preparation $\rho$ the identities and existence
criteria are those of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] and
[[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]]. In particular a mean exists
exactly when $\rho$ is concentrated on the domain of $|A|^{1/2}$ in the sense
of those items, and no preparation is equipped with finite moments
automatically.

**(d) Products of spreads.** For two assigned sharp observables $(A,u_{A})$
and $(B,u_{B})$ in a common preparation $\rho$ in which both spreads are
defined, the product $\Delta_{\rho}A\,\Delta_{\rho}B$ is a nonnegative real
number read in the product unit $u_{A}u_{B}$; for a pure preparation of a unit
vector in $D(A)\cap D(B)$ it is
$\|(A-a)\psi\|\,\|(B-b)\psi\|$ with the real means $a=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$
and $b=\langle B\psi,\psi\rangle$.

**(e) Reading and scope.** The spread $\Delta_{\rho}A$ is a property of the
pair (preparation, assigned observable): it is the standard deviation of the
outcome law that P2 assigns. It is not an apparatus resolution, not a
measurement error and not a disturbance of the preparation; those are further
objects that require a declared instrument or apparatus model and are not
introduced here. Clause (b) makes no claim that a preparation realizes a
specific laboratory state, that a laboratory procedure measures $A$ with
resolution $u_{A}$, or that the spread is observed in any experiment; the
identification of an apparatus with the pair $(A,u_{A})$ is a tested
identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7.
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] fixes the units in which the
displays are read.

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (a), (b), (c), and the coherent-state family of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-states]]; assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $Q$ and $P$ be the model's position and momentum observables with their declared units ($\mathrm m$ and $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$), let $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, let $\Delta_{\rho}A$ be the preparation spread of an assigned sharp observable in the reading of [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]], and write $\langle A\rangle_z:=\langle A\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle$ for the model's coherent preparation of label $z$. Then:

(a) **Coherent spreads.** For every $z\in\mathbb C$ the vector $\Psi_z$ lies in $D(Q)\cap D(P)$, the preparation spreads of $Q$ and $P$ in the pure preparation of $\Psi_z$ exist, and
$$\Delta_{\Psi_z}Q=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\frac{\hbar}{\ell\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_z}Q\,\Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\frac{\hbar}{2};$$

(b) **Position-momentum relation of the model.** Every unit vector $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$ satisfies
$$\Delta_{f}Q\,\Delta_{f}P\ge\frac{\hbar}{2},$$
read in the product unit $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{2}\mathrm s^{-1}$; consequently the value $\hbar/2$ attained in (a) is the minimum over the common domain, and it is attained by every coherent preparation;

(c) **Saturation.** For every $z\in\mathbb C$, with the centered vectors
$$x_z:=(Q-\langle Q\rangle_zI)\Psi_z,\qquad y_z:=(P-\langle P\rangle_zI)\Psi_z,$$
one has $\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=-i\hbar/2$; in particular $\operatorname{Re}\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=0$ and $x_z,y_z$ are linearly dependent, so $\|x_z\|\,\|y_z\|=|\langle x_z,y_z\rangle|=\hbar/2$;

(d) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P5, the adopted oscillator model, the cited preparation-moment and uncertainty results and the cited mathematics. They concern the spreads of the two separately assigned outcome laws of $Q$ and $P$ in one preparation; they introduce no joint outcome law of position and momentum, no measurement error, no disturbance of the preparation, no dynamics and no empirical value. Whether a laboratory preparation and apparatus realize the pair of observables and produce this spread is a tested identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7.

derivations.claim: [The ground vector] By [F1], $\psi_0=Dg_0$ with $g_0(y)=\pi^{-1/4}e^{-y^{2}/2}$, so its representative is $\psi_0(x)=\ell^{-1/2}\pi^{-1/4}e^{-x^{2}/(2\ell^{2})}$ and $\|\psi_0\|=\|g_0\|=1$ because $D$ is an isometry; $H_1\psi_0=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\psi_0$ and $\psi_0=\Psi_0$ are also from [F1].

[The position law] By [F2] and [F1], for every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ the position law of the ground preparation is $\mu^{Q}_{\psi_0}(B)=\int_{x^{-1}(B)}|\psi_0(x)|^{2}dx=\int_B\ell^{-1}\pi^{-1/2}e^{-x^{2}/\ell^{2}}dx$, so $f(x)=\ell^{-1}\pi^{-1/2}e^{-x^{2}/\ell^{2}}$ is its density, with $\int f=1$ because $|\psi_0|^{2}$ is a probability density.

[The momentum law] By [F4] and [F5], for every Borel $B$ the momentum law is $\mu^{P}_{\psi_0}(B)=\int_{g^{-1}(B)}|\mathcal F_2\psi_0(\xi)|^{2}d\xi=\int_B(2\pi\hbar)^{-1}|\mathcal F_2\psi_0(p/(2\pi\hbar))|^{2}dp$, using the substitution $p=2\pi\hbar\xi$ in the second step; hence the density is $g(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-1}|\mathcal F_2\psi_0(p/(2\pi\hbar))|^{2}$.

[The Fourier transform of the ground vector] By [F5] applied with $t=1/(2\pi\ell^{2})$, $\mathcal F_2(e^{-x^{2}/(2\ell^{2})})(\xi)=(\frac{1}{2\pi\ell^{2}})^{-1/2}e^{-2\pi^{2}\ell^{2}\xi^{2}}=\sqrt{2\pi}\,\ell\,e^{-2\pi^{2}\ell^{2}\xi^{2}}$, so by [F1] $\mathcal F_2\psi_0(\xi)=\ell^{-1/2}\pi^{-1/4}\sqrt{2\pi}\,\ell\,e^{-2\pi^{2}\ell^{2}\xi^{2}}=\sqrt{2\pi}\,\ell^{1/2}\pi^{-1/4}e^{-2\pi^{2}\ell^{2}\xi^{2}}$ and $|\mathcal F_2\psi_0(\xi)|^{2}=2\pi\ell\pi^{-1/2}e^{-4\pi^{2}\ell^{2}\xi^{2}}=2\sqrt\pi\,\ell\,e^{-4\pi^{2}\ell^{2}\xi^{2}}$.
[Clause (a)] By step 1.1 the ground vector has the displayed representative, is a unit vector, equals $\Psi_0$, and satisfies $H_1\psi_0=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\psi_0$.

[Clause (b)] By step 1.2 the position density is $f(x)=\ell^{-1}\pi^{-1/2}e^{-x^{2}/\ell^{2}}$, which equals the heat kernel $\Gamma(x,\ell^{2}/4)$; by [F3] it integrates to $1$, and its mean and second moment are those of $\Gamma(\cdot,\ell^{2}/4)$: $\int x f=0$ and $\int x^{2}f=2\cdot\frac{\ell^{2}}{4}=\frac{\ell^{2}}{2}$.

[Clause (c)] By steps 1.3 and 1.4, $g(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-1}\cdot2\sqrt\pi\,\ell\,e^{-4\pi^{2}\ell^{2}(p/(2\pi\hbar))^{2}}=(2\pi\hbar)^{-1}2\sqrt\pi\,\ell\,e^{-\ell^{2}p^{2}/\hbar^{2}}=\frac{\ell}{\hbar\sqrt\pi}e^{-\ell^{2}p^{2}/\hbar^{2}}$, which equals the heat kernel $\Gamma(p,\hbar^{2}/(4\ell^{2}))$; by [F3] it integrates to $1$ and has mean $0$ and second moment $2\cdot\frac{\hbar^{2}}{4\ell^{2}}=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2\ell^{2}}$.

[Clause (d)] By steps 2.2 and 2.3 the ground preparation has position variance $\ell^{2}/2$ and momentum variance $\hbar^{2}/(2\ell^{2})$, so by [F6] its spreads are $\Delta_{\psi_0}Q=\ell/\sqrt2$ and $\Delta_{\psi_0}P=\hbar/(\ell\sqrt2)$ with product $\hbar/2$; by [F6] this is the value of the coherent preparations, and by [[pthm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-fluctuations]] it is the minimum of the spread product over the common domain.

[Clause (e)] The computation used only the model's ground vector, the multiplication and Fourier forms of the model's position and momentum observables and the Gaussian heat-kernel facts; no measured distribution, apparatus or empirical value entered.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.2 computes the position law $\mu^{Q}_{\psi_0}(B)=\int_{B}f(x)\,dx$ for every Borel $B$, and step 1.3 the momentum law likewise; an empty Borel set therefore has probability $0$ by the cited scalar laws.

Step 1.1 shows $\psi_0$ has the strictly positive Gaussian representative, and steps 2.2-2.3 show both outcome densities are continuous, so the laws carry no atom at $x=0$ or $p=0$; step 3.1 computes the mean zero together with the positive variance $\ell^{2}/2$.

The example computes the law of the single ground vector $\psi_0$; step 1.1 identifies it as $\psi_0=\Psi_0$, the coherent state of label $0$, and step 3.1 saturates the product $\Delta Q\,\Delta P=\hbar/2$.

Step 3.1 gives strictly positive variances $\ell^{2}/2$ and $\hbar^{2}/(2\ell^{2})$ with $\ell>0$, so the ground preparation is not concentrated; step 4.1 records that no zero-spread degeneration occurs.

Steps 2.2-2.3 integrate the continuous densities over all Borel sets; the heat-kernel slices used in [F3] are evaluated only at $t>0$, and the excluded endpoint $t=0$ of the heat kernel is never used.
The Axiom of Countable Choice is assumed in the statement and used through the spectral, Plancherel, Fourier and heat-kernel suppliers cited as [F2]-[F5]; steps 1.1-4.1 invoke no further choice.

boundaries.reason: The example asserts equalities of vectors, laws and numbers (clauses (a)-(d)); no biconditional is asserted, so there is no forward direction.
No converse implication is asserted; the example does not claim that every preparation with these laws is the ground state.

risk_review.notes: Read all nine verification steps and current multiplier-PVM, Plancherel, Gaussian-transform, linear C1 change-of-variables, heat-kernel normalization/moment, coherent and spread supplier statements. The ground vector is the fixed psi0=Dg0 (not an arbitrary phase representative). Positive ell and hbar make both heat-kernel parameters positive. Fourier convention is exp(-2 pi i x xi), momentum p=2 pi hbar xi, Jacobian (2 pi hbar)^-1; squared transform yields exactly ell/(hbar sqrt(pi)) exp(-ell^2 p^2/hbar^2). Both laws normalize and their moments are absolutely integrable; second moments yield the claimed spreads. Reader changed contract citations only, carrier pre/post hashes coincide: audit enrichment, no mathematical defect or new item edit. Conditional laws, no measured distributions.

citations.quote:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] with parameters $m>0$, $\omega>0$ and action constant $\hbar>0$, and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, let $(g_n)$, $D$, $A$, $(\psi_n)$ and $H_1$ be the Hermite family, the unitary, the dimensionless diagonal operator, the scaled eigenbasis and the energy operator of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (a) and (b), so that $\psi_n=Dg_n$ and $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ is the model's one-dimensional assigned energy observable of the model definition clause (c). Put
$$N_\psi:=DND^{-1},\qquad a_\psi:=DaD^{-1},\qquad a^\dagger_\psi:=Da^\dagger D^{-1},$$
where $N$ is the number operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]] and $N_\psi$ is the assigned excitation-number observable with unit $1/\mathrm{count}$ of the model definition clause (c); these are the number and ladder operators transported from that lemma, with domains $D(N_\psi)=\{Dx:x\in D(N)\}$, $D(a_\psi)=\{Dx:x\in D(a)\}$ and $D(a^\dagger_\psi)=\{Dx:x\in D(a^\dagger)\}$. Write $E_n:=\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)$ and, for the three-dimensional realization of the model definition clause (d), let $(H_3,\mathrm J)$ and $(\psi_N)_{N\in\mathbb N^3}$ be its assigned energy observable and its product eigenbasis. Then:

(a) **Spectrum, eigenbasis and simplicity.** $D(H_1)=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:\sum_nn^{2}|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}<\infty\}$, the family $(\psi_n)$ is a complete orthonormal family of $\mathcal H_1$ and a core for $H_1$, $H_1\psi_n=E_n\psi_n$, and the spectrum and eigenspaces are
$$\sigma(H_1)=\{E_n:n\in\mathbb N\},\qquad \ker(H_1-E_nI)=\mathbb C\psi_n\quad(n\in\mathbb N);$$
the ground energy is $E_0=\hbar\omega/2$ and the gap between consecutive levels is $E_{n+1}-E_n=\hbar\omega$;

(b) **Excitation reading.** $H_1=\hbar\omega\bigl(N_\psi+\tfrac12I\bigr)$ with common domain $D(H_1)=D(N_\psi)$; $N_\psi$ is self-adjoint with spectrum $\mathbb N$ and eigenbasis $(\psi_n)$; $a_\psi$ and $a^\dagger_\psi$ are closed with $a_\psi^{*}=a^\dagger_\psi$, and on the eigenbasis
$$a_\psi\psi_n=\sqrt n\,\psi_{n-1}\ (n\ge1),\qquad a_\psi\psi_0=0,\qquad a^\dagger_\psi\psi_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,\psi_{n+1},\qquad N_\psi\psi_n=n\psi_n;$$
the eigenspace of $N_\psi$ at each $n\in\mathbb N$ is exactly $\mathbb C\psi_n$, so its nonzero eigenvectors are precisely the nonzero scalar multiples of the $\psi_n$; the outcome law of $N_\psi$ in the pure preparation of $\psi_n$ is the point mass $\delta_n$;

(c) **Energy outcome law.** For every unit $f\in\mathcal H_1$ the outcome law of the assigned energy observable $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ in the pure preparation of $f$ is purely atomic with
$$\mu^{H_1}_f\bigl(\{E_n\}\bigr)=|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}\quad(n\in\mathbb N),\qquad \mu^{H_1}_f(B)=\sum_{n:\,E_n\in B}|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}$$
for every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$, and $\mu^{H_1}_f(\sigma(H_1))=1$; in particular the law has no mass outside $\{E_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$, and $E_n$ is an atom of the law of $f$ exactly when $\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\ne0$;

(d) **Three-dimensional isotropic realization.** The energy observable $(H_3,\mathrm J)$ of the model definition clause (d) has spectrum $\sigma(H_3)=\{\hbar\omega(M+\tfrac32):M\in\mathbb N\}$; for every $M\in\mathbb N$ the eigenspace $\ker(H_3-\hbar\omega(M+\frac32)I)$ has the orthonormal basis $\{\psi_N:N\in\mathbb N^{3},\ n_1+n_2+n_3=M\}$ and dimension $(M+1)(M+2)/2$; the ground energy is $\tfrac32\hbar\omega$;

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P4, P5, the adopted oscillator model and the cited mathematics. They concern the eigenvalue list, the eigenbasis, the excitation operators and the atomic outcome law of the model's assigned energy observable; they assert no measured spectral line, no numerical value of $m$, $\omega$ or $\hbar$, no apparatus realization, no selection rule and no transition rate. The identification of a laboratory resonance or spectral line with an eigenvalue difference of this model is a tested identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not a consequence of this theorem.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix real parameters $m>0$, $\omega>0$, $\hbar>0$, put $\ell:=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}>0$, and let $g_0,P,(g_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be the Hermite data of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-recurrence]] in $L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$, so that $(g_n)$ is a complete orthonormal family by [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-completeness]]. Define

$$D:L^2(\mathbb R,dy)\to L^2(\mathbb R,dx),\qquad (Df)(x):=\ell^{-1/2}f(x/\ell),$$

and let $A$ be the self-adjoint diagonal operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]] for the complete orthonormal family $(g_n)$ and the eigenvalues $\lambda_n=2n+1$, with the core $P$ and spectrum $\{2n+1:n\in\mathbb N\}$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-spectrum]]).

Then:

(a) $D$ is a linear isometry of $L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$ onto $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$ with two-sided inverse $(D^{-1}g)(y)=\ell^{1/2}g(\ell y)$; the functions $\psi_n:=Dg_n$, $\psi_n(x)=\ell^{-1/2}g_n(x/\ell)$, form a complete orthonormal family of $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$;

(b) the operator

$$H_{\mathrm{osc}}:=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\,DAD^{-1},\qquad D(H_{\mathrm{osc}}):=\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R,dx):D^{-1}f\in D(A)\},$$

is self-adjoint, satisfies $H_{\mathrm{osc}}\psi_n=\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)\psi_n$ for every $n$, and has

$$D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})=\Bigl\{f:\sum_n\hbar^2\omega^2(n+\tfrac12)^2|c_n|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad H_{\mathrm{osc}}f=\sum_n\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)c_n\psi_n,$$

where $c_n:=\langle D^{-1}f,g_n\rangle=\langle f,\psi_n\rangle$; its spectrum is $\sigma(H_{\mathrm{osc}})=\{\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12):n\in\mathbb N\}$, its ground energy is $\hbar\omega/2$ with eigenvector $\psi_0$, and $\langle H_{\mathrm{osc}}f,f\rangle\ge\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\|f\|^2$ for every $f\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$;

(c) $D(P)=\operatorname{span}\{\psi_n\}$ is a core for $H_{\mathrm{osc}}$, and for every polynomial $p$ the function $f:=D(pg_0)$ is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R$ with

$$H_{\mathrm{osc}}f=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}f''+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2f$$

pointwise on $\mathbb R$;

(d) for every $f\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ and every test function $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$,

$$\int_{\mathbb R}(H_{\mathrm{osc}}f)(x)\varphi(x)\,dx=\int_{\mathbb R}f(x)\Bigl(-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\varphi''(x)+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2\varphi(x)\Bigr)dx,$$

so $H_{\mathrm{osc}}$ is the self-adjoint realization of the differential expression $-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\frac{d^2}{dx^2}+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2$ in the weak sense; no identification of $D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ with a separately defined maximal differential-operator domain is asserted.

All parameters enter as positive real numbers; no physical identification of $m,\omega,\hbar$ with measured quantities is made.

**(a) Adopted framework assumptions.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, in the readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]], [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix real model parameters $m>0$ (mass parameter, unit $\mathrm{kg}$), $\omega>0$ (angular frequency, unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$) and the action constant $\hbar>0$ (unit $\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$) of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)4, and put
$$\ell:=\sqrt{\frac{\hbar}{m\omega}}>0\qquad\text{(unit }\mathrm m\text{),}$$
the model's length scale.

**(b) One-dimensional realization.** Write $\mathcal H_1:=L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx;\mathbb C)$ for the model's one-dimensional state space, the complex Hilbert space of almost-everywhere classes with inner product linear in the first argument, taken in the scalar reading $r=1$ of the component-valued space of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] for $d=1$. The model's **position** and **momentum** are the operators of that lemma at $d=1$, $r=1$, namely
$$Q:=M_x,\qquad D(Q)=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:xf\in L^{2}\},\qquad (Qf)(x)=xf(x),$$
$$P:=-i\hbar D_x,\qquad D(P)=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:\text{the weak derivative }D_xf\text{ lies in }L^{2}\},\qquad Pf=-i\hbar D_xf,$$
which are densely defined and self-adjoint with exactly these domains; the model assigns to $(Q,\mathrm m)$ and to $(P,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$ the status of assigned sharp observables in the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), with outcome laws read from P2.

**(c) Energy and excitation-number observables.** Let $g_0,(g_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ and the unitary $D:L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)\to L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$ be the Hermite data and scaling map of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (a), (b) for the parameters $m,\omega,\hbar$. Put $\mathscr P_y:=\{p g_0:p\in\mathbb C[y]\}\subseteq L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$; the Hermite recurrence [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-recurrence]] identifies this polynomial-Gaussian space with $\operatorname{span}\{g_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$, and its scaled image $\mathscr P_x:=D(\mathscr P_y)=\operatorname{span}\{\psi_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$ is the core supplied by the scaling theorem. Let $A$ be the diagonal operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]] for the family $(g_n)$ and eigenvalues $2n+1$. The model's **energy operator** is
$$H_1:=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\,D A D^{-1},\qquad D(H_1):=\{f\in\mathcal H_1:D^{-1}f\in D(A)\},$$
the operator of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clause (b); its exact domain, action, spectrum and eigenbasis are those established there. The model assigns to $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ the status of assigned energy observable of the isolated system in the sense of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clauses (a) and (b): the model's flow is $U(t)=\exp(-itH_1/\hbar)$ and the model's Schroedinger dynamics is the one of that definition. Let $N$ be the self-adjoint number operator on $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$ of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]] for the Hermite family $(g_n)$, and set $N_\psi:=DND^{-1}$. Its transported domain and action are
$$D(N_\psi)=\Bigl\{f\in\mathcal H_1:\sum_n n^2|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad N_\psi f=\sum_n n\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\psi_n,$$
with the series converging in $\mathcal H_1$; it is self-adjoint by [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-unitary-transport-of-spectral-pvms]] clauses (a), (d). The model assigns to $(N_\psi,1/\mathrm{count})$ the status of its dimensionless excitation-number observable; here $\mathrm{count}$ denotes one excitation count and is dimensionless, so the spectral coordinate $n$ records $n$ excitations, and its outcome laws are read by P2. On the scaled polynomial-Gaussian core $\mathscr P_x$ the operator $H_1$ is the self-adjoint realization of the quadratic expression: for every $f\in\mathscr P_x$,
$$H_1f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}f''+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}f$$
pointwise, and for every $f\in D(H_1)$ the weak identity $\int (H_1f)\varphi\,dx=\int f\bigl(-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\varphi''+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}\varphi\bigr)dx$ holds for every $\varphi\in C_c^{\infty}(\mathbb R)$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (c), (d)). The formal differential expression $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\frac{d^{2}}{dx^{2}}+\frac{m\omega^{2}}{2}x^{2}$ is the model's **quadratic potential energy plus kinetic energy** reading; no identification of $D(H_1)$ with any independently defined maximal differential-operator domain, and no separate quadratic-form-domain characterization, is asserted.

**(d) Three-dimensional isotropic realization.** For the spinless reading $s=0$ of the massive-particle model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]], with state space $\mathcal H_3:=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dx;\mathbb C)$, position operators $Q_j$ and momentum operators $P_k$ ($j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$) with the domains and units of that definition, the model with common frequency $\omega$ has **energy operator** $H_3$ equal to the diagonal operator $H$ of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-multidimensional-oscillator-completeness]] clause (c) for $d=3$, $m_j=m$, $\omega_j=\omega$, a self-adjoint operator on $\mathcal H_3$ with the domain, spectrum and core displayed there. **(e) Physical reading and scope.** Clause (c) defines the model quantities that the page calls the energy and excitation number; it is a **model assumption** that the energy of the declared isolated particle is the assigned observable $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ and that $(N_\psi,1/\mathrm{count})$ is its excitation-number observable. The additive constant of the potential energy is removed at the minimum: for a one-dimensional potential-energy function $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^2$, with values in joules for position $x$ in metres, suppose $V$ has a non-degenerate local minimum at $0$, meaning $V'(0)=0$ and $V''(0)>0$. Taylor's theorem gives $V(x)-V(0)=\frac{1}{2}V''(0)x^{2}+o(x^{2})$ as $x\to0$; the oscillator model approximates this shifted potential-energy function by its quadratic term and sets $m\omega^{2}=V''(0)$. The oscillator's quantum ground energy in this convention is $\hbar\omega/2$. With only the stated $C^2$ regularity, the remainder is $o(x^2)$; no quantitative finite-amplitude error bound is asserted on this page (Binney §3.1, cited in the references). No measured value, no laboratory identification and no derivation of $m$ or $\omega$ from any microscopic or environmental theory is asserted. The model contains no damping, no external driving, no time-dependent parameters, no coupling to electromagnetic fields or radiation, no spin-dependent force, no anharmonic term, no relativistic correction and no boundary or many-body effect; those are separate model assumptions belonging to their own items. The parameters $m$ and $\omega$ are model parameters of dimensions $\mu$ and $\tau^{-1}$ in the conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and all displayed quantities are read in the units fixed there.

**(f) Status.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the objects used by the theorems of this page and record the readings of P1, P2, P4 and P5 in the model's terminology. They assert no preparation or apparatus model, no detection model, no joint outcome law of position and momentum and no empirical result.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

**(a) Dimensions.** Write $\ell$, $\tau$, $\mu$, $\vartheta$ for the four independent dimension symbols of length, duration, mass and electric charge. A **dimension** is an element of $\mathbb Q^{4}$, written $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ with $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb Q$; products and inverses of dimensions are componentwise addition and negation, and the dimensionless dimension $\ell^{0}\tau^{0}\mu^{0}\vartheta^{0}$ is abbreviated $1$. The conventions assign to each quantity of the framework a dimension $[X]$, subject to $[XY]=[X][Y]$, $[X/Y]=[X][Y]^{-1}$ and $[dX/du]=[X][u]^{-1}$, with sums meaningful only between quantities of equal dimension, in which case the sum carries that dimension. For a rational power $q$, dimension powers mean $[X]^q=\ell^{qa}\tau^{qb}\mu^{qc}\vartheta^{qd}$ when $[X]=\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$. Rational exponents include the half-integer wave-function dimensions in clause (d); the integer-exponent dimensions form the subgroup $\mathbb Z^4$. These are consistency requirements on the conventions, not laws of nature.

**(b) Reference units.** The **metre** (m), **second** (s), **kilogram** (kg) and **coulomb** (C) are the reference units of length, duration, mass and charge; a quantity of dimension $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ is expressed in the unit $\mathrm m^{a}\mathrm s^{b}\mathrm kg^{c}\mathrm C^{d}$. Coordinates of an inertial frame are read with the time coordinate $t$ in seconds, $[t]=\tau$, and the spatial coordinates $x_{i}$ in metres, $[x_{i}]=\ell$; slice distances of the arena are read in metres.

**(c) Defining constants of the current SI.** The framework keeps $\hbar$ explicit. In the current SI the constants $h$, $c$ and $e$ are exact defining constants, with the values $h=6{,}626\,070\,15\times10^{-34}$ J s, $c=2{,}99792458\times10^{8}$ m s$^{-1}$ and $e=1{,}602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}$ C, and $\hbar:=h/(2\pi)$. These are real scalar constants with dimensions and units $[h]=[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$ (J s), $[c]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ (m s$^{-1}$), and $[e]=\vartheta$ (C). The vacuum permeability $\mu_{0}$ is a positive real scalar that is experimentally determined in the current SI, with $[\mu_{0}]=\mu\ell\vartheta^{-2}$ (N A$^{-2}$ = H m$^{-1}$); $\varepsilon_{0}:=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1}$ is a positive real scalar with $[\varepsilon_{0}]=\mu^{-1}\ell^{-3}\tau^{2}\vartheta^{2}$ (F m$^{-1}$). These are unit-convention statements of the SI, not measurements reported by this framework; $c$ enters the framework only through the separate radiation assumptions adopted on their own pages, not in the nonrelativistic spacetime of [[def-nrqm-framework-newtonian-spacetime]].

**(d) Dimensions and types of the framework's quantities.** The dimension map is fixed on the following quantities.

1. State quantities: a position wave function of a system with $d$ spatial dimensions and $r$ internal components is an almost-everywhere equivalence class in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with dimension $\ell^{-d/2}$, its norm $\|\psi\|$ is dimensionless, and an abstract normalized state and the density operators of the state postulate are dimensionless.
2. Probability: the outcome probability $\mu(B)$ of the observable postulate is a dimensionless number; a position density $|\psi|^{2}$ has dimension $\ell^{-d}$; a momentum wave function normalized against $\mathrm d^{d}p$ has dimension $(\mu\ell\tau^{-1})^{-d/2}$; an amplitude for a finite outcome is a dimensionless complex number, while an amplitude read against a detector coordinate carries the square-root of the inverse of the detector measure.
3. Frame parameters ([[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]]): $[b]=\tau$, $[a_{i}]=\ell$, $[v_{i}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ and $[R_{ij}]=1$.
4. Mechanical quantities: action $[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; energy and the Hamiltonian eigenvalues $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$; momentum $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$; position components $\ell$; angular momentum and spin $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; mass $\mu$; velocity of a free spinless model $\ell\tau^{-1}$; force $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$; a real potential energy $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$.
5. Probability current: $j$ has dimension $\ell^{1-d}\tau^{-1}$; it is a probability flux, not a charge flux.
6. Electric quantities of the model parameters: charge has dimension $\vartheta$; a magnetic moment has dimension $\ell^{2}\vartheta\tau^{-1}$, equivalently $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{2}=\mathrm J\,\mathrm T^{-1}$, and a gyromagnetic parameter $\gamma$ in the relation $\boldsymbol\mu=\gamma\mathbf S$ has dimension $\mu^{-1}\vartheta$, equivalently $\mathrm s^{-1}\mathrm T^{-1}$; these quantities appear only in the model assumptions that introduce them.
7. Statistical quantities: a mean has the dimension of its outcome coordinate, a variance the square of it and a standard deviation it; a mean, variance or higher moment exists only when the corresponding moment of the outcome probability is finite, so a symbolic average is not a number unless that integrability is established. Angles and phases are dimensionless under the radian convention.
8. Quantities of later extension assumptions - radiation frequencies and energies, electric dipole moments, cross sections, temperatures and entropies - are declared with their dimensions and units by the items that introduce those assumptions, under the rules fixed here; they are not part of the present list.

**(e) Conventions only.** No numerical value of any model parameter is fixed by this item: no mass, charge, spin label, potential or measured constant is asserted, and natural-unit shorthand (for example setting $\hbar=1$ or $c=1$) is read as an abbreviation for the corresponding SI-dimensioned statement with the constant restored.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Define

$$D:L^2(\mathbb R,dy)\to L^2(\mathbb R,dx),\qquad (Df)(x):=\ell^{-1/2}f(x/\ell),$$

and let $A$ be the self-adjoint diagonal operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]] for the complete orthonormal family $(g_n)$ and the eigenvalues $\lambda_n=2n+1$, with the core $P$ and spectrum $\{2n+1:n\in\mathbb N\}$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-spectrum]]).

Then:

(a) $D$ is a linear isometry of $L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$ onto $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$ with two-sided inverse $(D^{-1}g)(y)=\ell^{1/2}g(\ell y)$; the functions $\psi_n:=Dg_n$, $\psi_n(x)=\ell^{-1/2}g_n(x/\ell)$, form a complete orthonormal family of $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$;

(b) the operator

$$H_{\mathrm{osc}}:=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\,DAD^{-1},\qquad D(H_{\mathrm{osc}}):=\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R,dx):D^{-1}f\in D(A)\},$$

is self-adjoint, satisfies $H_{\mathrm{osc}}\psi_n=\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)\psi_n$ for every $n$, and has

$$D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})=\Bigl\{f:\sum_n\hbar^2\omega^2(n+\tfrac12)^2|c_n|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad H_{\mathrm{osc}}f=\sum_n\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)c_n\psi_n,$$

where $c_n:=\langle D^{-1}f,g_n\rangle=\langle f,\psi_n\rangle$; its spectrum is $\sigma(H_{\mathrm{osc}})=\{\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12):n\in\mathbb N\}$, its ground energy is $\hbar\omega/2$ with eigenvector $\psi_0$, and $\langle H_{\mathrm{osc}}f,f\rangle\ge\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\|f\|^2$ for every $f\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$;

(c) $D(P)=\operatorname{span}\{\psi_n\}$ is a core for $H_{\mathrm{osc}}$, and for every polynomial $p$ the function $f:=D(pg_0)$ is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R$ with

$$H_{\mathrm{osc}}f=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}f''+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2f$$

pointwise on $\mathbb R$;

(d) for every $f\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ and every test function $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$,

$$\int_{\mathbb R}(H_{\mathrm{osc}}f)(x)\varphi(x)\,dx=\int_{\mathbb R}f(x)\Bigl(-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\varphi''(x)+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2\varphi(x)\Bigr)dx,$$

so $H_{\mathrm{osc}}$ is the self-adjoint realization of the differential expression $-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\frac{d^2}{dx^2}+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2$ in the weak sense; no identification of $D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ with a separately defined maximal differential-operator domain is asserted.

All parameters enter as positive real numbers; no physical identification of $m,\omega,\hbar$ with measured quantities is made.

derivations.claim: [Ladder images] By [F1], $a_\psi\psi_0=0$, $a_\psi\psi_1=\sqrt1\psi_0=\psi_0$, $a_\psi\psi_2=\sqrt2\psi_1$, $a^\dagger_\psi\psi_0=\sqrt1\psi_1=\psi_1$ and $a^\dagger_\psi\psi_1=\sqrt2\psi_2$.

[Matrix elements] By [F1] and [F3], for $n\ge1$ and every $m$, $\langle\psi_m,a_\psi\psi_n\rangle=\sqrt n\langle\psi_m,\psi_{n-1}\rangle=\sqrt n\,\delta_{m,n-1}$, $\langle\psi_m,a^\dagger_\psi\psi_n\rangle=\sqrt{n+1}\langle\psi_m,\psi_{n+1}\rangle=\sqrt{n+1}\,\delta_{m,n+1}$, and $\langle a_\psi\psi_n,a_\psi\psi_m\rangle=\sqrt{nm}\langle\psi_{n-1},\psi_{m-1}\rangle=n\,\delta_{nm}$ for $n,m\ge1$. At $n=0$, $a^\dagger_\psi\psi_0=\psi_1$ gives $\langle\psi_m,a^\dagger_\psi\psi_0\rangle=\delta_{m,1}$. If $n=0$ or $m=0$, one annihilation image vanishes by $a_\psi\psi_0=0$, so the pairing is zero, equal to $n\delta_{nm}$.

[Number and energy laws of the eigenstates] By [F1], $N_\psi\psi_n=n\psi_n$ and the number law of the unit eigenvector $\psi_n$ is $\delta_n$; likewise the energy law of the unit eigenvector is $\mu^{H_1}_{\psi_n}(\{E_n\})=|\langle\psi_n,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}=1$ by [F1] and [F3], so the preparation carries exactly $n$ excitations and the energy value $E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)$.

[Clause (a)] Taking norms in the images of step 1.1 and using $\|\psi_k\|=1$ of [F3] gives $\|a_\psi\psi_1\|=\|\psi_0\|=1$, $\|a_\psi\psi_2\|=\sqrt2\|\psi_1\|=\sqrt2$, $\|a^\dagger_\psi\psi_0\|=\|\psi_1\|=1$ and $\|a^\dagger_\psi\psi_1\|=\sqrt2\|\psi_2\|=\sqrt2$.
[Clause (b)] The displays of clause (b) are exactly the identities computed in step 1.2.

[Clause (d)] By [F1], $a_\psi\psi_0=0$ and $a^\dagger_\psi\psi_0=\psi_1\ne0$, so $a_\psi\ne a^\dagger_\psi$. Since $a_\psi^{*}=a^\dagger_\psi$ and $(a^\dagger_\psi)^{*}=a_\psi$ by [F1], neither operator is self-adjoint. By [F2] the assigned sharp observables are the self-adjoint operators listed; hence the norms computed in clauses (a) and (b) are norms of operator images and not outcome values of any assigned sharp observable of the model.
[Clause (e)] The computation used the model's eigenbasis and ladder operators and the orthonormality of the eigenbasis; it produced no measurement record and no claim about a laboratory preparation.
