Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (a), (b), (c), and the coherent-state family of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-states]]; assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $U(t)=\exp(-itH_1/\hbar)$ be the model's flow, let $\Psi_z$ be the coherent state of label $z\in\mathbb C$, put $z(t):=ze^{-i\omega t}$, and define $x_0:=\sqrt2\,\ell\operatorname{Re}z$, $p_0:=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z$ for every $z\in\mathbb C$. Then:

(a) **Coherent evolution.** For every $t\in\mathbb R$, $U(t)$ is a bijective linear isometry of $\mathcal H_1$ and
$$U(t)\Psi_z=e^{-i\omega t/2}\,\Psi_{z(t)};$$
consequently the preparation $[\Psi_z]$ evolves under the model's Schroedinger dynamics to the coherent preparation $[\Psi_{z(t)}]$, and the labels of the evolved family rotate with angular frequency $\omega$;

(b) **Classical mean motion.** The preparation means of position and momentum at time $t$ are
$$\langle Q\rangle_{z(t)}=\sqrt2\,\ell\operatorname{Re}z(t),\qquad \langle P\rangle_{z(t)}=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z(t),$$
equivalently, for every $t\in\mathbb R$, $x(t)=x_0\cos\omega t+\frac{p_0}{m\omega}\sin\omega t$ and $p(t)=p_0\cos\omega t-m\omega x_0\sin\omega t$ with $x(t):=\langle Q\rangle_{z(t)}$, $p(t):=\langle P\rangle_{z(t)}$; these functions are differentiable with $\dot x(t)=\frac{p(t)}{m}$ and $\dot p(t)=-m\omega^{2}x(t)$ for every $t$, so the means follow the classical harmonic motion of frequency $\omega$ through $(x_0,p_0)$;

(c) **Stationary fluctuations.** For every $t\in\mathbb R$ the evolved preparation has
$$\Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}Q=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}P=\frac{\hbar}{\ell\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}Q\,\Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}P=\frac{\hbar}{2};$$
the position and momentum spreads and their product are constant along the evolution;

(d) **Energy statistics.** The mean and the outcome law of the assigned energy observable in the coherent preparation are
$$\langle H_1\rangle_{z}=\hbar\omega\Bigl(|z|^{2}+\frac12\Bigr),\qquad \mu^{H_1}_{\Psi_z}\bigl(\{\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)\}\bigr)=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}\quad(n\in\mathbb N),$$
the pushforward under $n\mapsto\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)$ of the **Poisson law** on $\mathbb N$ with parameter $s:=|z|^2$, defined by the weights $p_n=e^{-s}s^n/n!$, with $s^0=1$ also at $s=0$; consequently $\Delta_{\Psi_z}H_1=\hbar\omega|z|$;

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P4, P5, the adopted oscillator model, the model's spectrum theorem, the coherent-state fluctuation theorem and the cited mathematics. They concern the exact evolution of the model's coherent preparations and the statistics of its assigned observables; no measurement record, no apparatus realization, no damping or driving and no empirical value is asserted, and the identification of the mean motion with the motion of a laboratory oscillator is a tested identification under P7.

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (a), (b), (c), and the coherent-state family of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-states]]; assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $Q$ and $P$ be the model's position and momentum observables with their declared units ($\mathrm m$ and $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$), let $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, let $\Delta_{\rho}A$ be the preparation spread of an assigned sharp observable in the reading of [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]], and write $\langle A\rangle_z:=\langle A\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle$ for the model's coherent preparation of label $z$. Then:

(a) **Coherent spreads.** For every $z\in\mathbb C$ the vector $\Psi_z$ lies in $D(Q)\cap D(P)$, the preparation spreads of $Q$ and $P$ in the pure preparation of $\Psi_z$ exist, and
$$\Delta_{\Psi_z}Q=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\frac{\hbar}{\ell\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_z}Q\,\Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\frac{\hbar}{2};$$

(b) **Position-momentum relation of the model.** Every unit vector $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$ satisfies
$$\Delta_{f}Q\,\Delta_{f}P\ge\frac{\hbar}{2},$$
read in the product unit $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{2}\mathrm s^{-1}$; consequently the value $\hbar/2$ attained in (a) is the minimum over the common domain, and it is attained by every coherent preparation;

(c) **Saturation.** For every $z\in\mathbb C$, with the centered vectors
$$x_z:=(Q-\langle Q\rangle_zI)\Psi_z,\qquad y_z:=(P-\langle P\rangle_zI)\Psi_z,$$
one has $\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=-i\hbar/2$; in particular $\operatorname{Re}\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=0$ and $x_z,y_z$ are linearly dependent, so $\|x_z\|\,\|y_z\|=|\langle x_z,y_z\rangle|=\hbar/2$;

(d) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P5, the adopted oscillator model, the cited preparation-moment and uncertainty results and the cited mathematics. They concern the spreads of the two separately assigned outcome laws of $Q$ and $P$ in one preparation; they introduce no joint outcome law of position and momentum, no measurement error, no disturbance of the preparation, no dynamics and no empirical value. Whether a laboratory preparation and apparatus realize the pair of observables and produce this spread is a tested identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7.

For real $x,y$, $\exp(x+iy)=e^x(\cos y+i\sin y)$ and $|\exp(x+iy)|=e^x$. In particular $e^{i\pi}+1=0$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]], [[thm-eulers-formula]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]], [[thm-pythagorean-and-parity-identities-for-all-six-trigonometric-functions]], [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]], [[def-pi-via-first-positive-cosine-zero]].

For every real $x$, $\sin ^2x+\cos ^2x=1$, $\sin(-x)=-\sin x$, and $\cos(-x)=\cos x$. Wherever the displayed quotients are defined, $\tan(-x)=-\tan x$, $\cot(-x)=-\cot x$, $\sec(-x)=\sec x$, $\csc(-x)=-\csc x$, $1+\tan^2x=\sec^2x$, and $1+\cot^2x=\csc^2x$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]], [[def-tangent-cotangent-secant-cosecant]].

For every real $x$,
$$\sin(x+\pi/2)=\cos x,\quad\cos(x+\pi/2)=-\sin x,\quad\sin(x+\pi)=-\sin x,\quad\cos(x+\pi)=-\cos x.$$
In particular,
$$\sin(\pi/2)=1,\quad\cos(\pi/2)=0,\quad\sin\pi=0,\quad\cos\pi=-1.$$

**(a) Setting.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the
observable and probability postulate P2 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned sharp observable with
declared unit $u_{A}$ and outcome law $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ in a preparation
$\rho$, in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b).

**(b) Preparation variance.** When the mean
$m(\rho):=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and the second
moment $\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ of the outcome
law are finite, the **preparation variance** of $(A,u_{A})$ in $\rho$ is
$$\operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(A):=\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\rho)\bigr)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda),$$
read in the square $u_{A}^{2}$ of the declared unit, and the **preparation
spread** is $\Delta_{\rho}A:=\operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(A)^{1/2}\ge0$, read in
the unit $u_{A}$. When either quantity is not finite the variance and the
spread of the pair in $\rho$ are **not defined**; the definition does not
extend them by $+\infty$.

**(c) Values and hypotheses.** The variance and its hypotheses are exactly
those of the moment theorem: for a pure preparation of a unit vector
$\psi\in D(A)$ the spread is $\Delta_{\psi}A=\|(A-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle I)\psi\|$,
equal to $\bigl(\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}\bigr)^{1/2}$
when $\psi\in D(A^{2})$; for a preparation $\rho$ the identities and existence
criteria are those of [[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] and
[[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]]. In particular a mean exists
exactly when $\rho$ is concentrated on the domain of $|A|^{1/2}$ in the sense
of those items, and no preparation is equipped with finite moments
automatically.

**(d) Products of spreads.** For two assigned sharp observables $(A,u_{A})$
and $(B,u_{B})$ in a common preparation $\rho$ in which both spreads are
defined, the product $\Delta_{\rho}A\,\Delta_{\rho}B$ is a nonnegative real
number read in the product unit $u_{A}u_{B}$; for a pure preparation of a unit
vector in $D(A)\cap D(B)$ it is
$\|(A-a)\psi\|\,\|(B-b)\psi\|$ with the real means $a=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$
and $b=\langle B\psi,\psi\rangle$.

**(e) Reading and scope.** The spread $\Delta_{\rho}A$ is a property of the
pair (preparation, assigned observable): it is the standard deviation of the
outcome law that P2 assigns. It is not an apparatus resolution, not a
measurement error and not a disturbance of the preparation; those are further
objects that require a declared instrument or apparatus model and are not
introduced here. Clause (b) makes no claim that a preparation realizes a
specific laboratory state, that a laboratory procedure measures $A$ with
resolution $u_{A}$, or that the spread is observed in any experiment; the
identification of an apparatus with the pair $(A,u_{A})$ is a tested
identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7.
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] fixes the units in which the
displays are read.

Let $U(t)=\exp(-itH_1/\hbar)$ be the model's flow, let $\Psi_z$ be the coherent state of label $z\in\mathbb C$, put $z(t):=ze^{-i\omega t}$, and define $x_0:=\sqrt2\,\ell\operatorname{Re}z$, $p_0:=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z$ for every $z\in\mathbb C$. Then:

derivations.claim: [The evolved family] By [F1] applied with $w=z$ and $s=t$, $\Psi_z(t)=U(t)\Psi_z=e^{-i\omega t/2}\Psi_{z(t)}$ with $z(t)=ze^{-i\omega t}$, and the means and spreads of the evolved preparation are those of the coherent label $z(t)$.

[The complex label in real form] By [F2], $e^{-i\omega t}=\cos\omega t-i\sin\omega t$, so $z(t)=z(\cos\omega t-i\sin\omega t)$ has real part $z_1\cos\omega t+z_2\sin\omega t$ and imaginary part $z_2\cos\omega t-z_1\sin\omega t$, and $\cos^{2}\omega t+\sin^{2}\omega t=1$; also $e^{-2\pi i}=1$.

[Clause (a)] By step 1.1 and [F2], $z(t+2\pi/\omega)=ze^{-i\omega t}e^{-2\pi i}=z(t)$ and $e^{-i\omega(t+2\pi/\omega)/2}=e^{-i\omega t/2}e^{-i\pi}=-e^{-i\omega t/2}$, so $U(2\pi/\omega)\Psi_z=-\Psi_z$; a global phase does not change the pure preparation, hence $[U(2\pi/\omega)\Psi_z]=[\Psi_z]$ and $[\Psi_z(t+2\pi/\omega)]=[\Psi_z(t)]$ for every $t$.

[Clause (b)] By step 1.1 and [F1], $x(t)=\sqrt2\ell\operatorname{Re}z(t)$ and $p(t)=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z(t)$; substituting the real and imaginary parts of step 1.2 and using $x_0=\sqrt2\ell z_1$, $\frac{p_0}{m\omega}=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar z_2}{\ell m\omega}=\sqrt2\ell z_2$, $m\omega x_0=\sqrt2 m\omega\ell z_1=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar z_1}{\ell}$ by $\ell^{2}=\hbar/(m\omega)$ gives the two displayed closed forms; at $t=0$ they read $x_0,p_0$, and at $t=\frac{\pi}{2\omega}$ they read $\frac{p_0}{m\omega}$ and $-m\omega x_0$ by the values in [F2]. For the ellipse, the closed forms give $\frac{x(t)^{2}}{2\ell^{2}}=(z_1\cos\omega t+z_2\sin\omega t)^{2}$ and $\frac{\ell^{2}p(t)^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}=(z_2\cos\omega t-z_1\sin\omega t)^{2}$; adding, the cross terms cancel and $\cos^{2}\omega t+\sin^{2}\omega t=1$ gives the sum $z_1^{2}+z_2^{2}=|z|^{2}$ for every $t$.

[Clause (c)] By step 1.1 the evolved preparation is the coherent preparation of label $z(t)$, so [F1] gives $\Delta_{\Psi_z(t)}Q=\ell/\sqrt2$, $\Delta_{\Psi_z(t)}P=\hbar/(\ell\sqrt2)$ and product $\hbar/2$ for every $t$.

[Clause (d)] By [F3] the quantities $x(t)$, $p(t)$ are outcome-law means of the model's position and momentum observables in the evolving preparation, and the spreads are outcome-law spreads; no measurement record, apparatus model or empirical value entered the computation.

boundaries.reason: The trajectory data are computed from one fixed nonzero label and real $t$; no family, sum or index set is quantified, so no empty case occurs.

boundaries.evidence: The statement fixes $|z|>0$, and steps 1.1-3.1 never divide by $|z|$: step 2.2 uses only $z_1,z_2$ and $\ell$, and the degenerate trajectory $z=0$ is treated in the companion fluctuation theorem [F1].

The computation concerns the single label $z$ and its phase-space point $(x_0,p_0)$; step 2.2 evaluates the closed forms at $t=0$ and at the quarter period, so the single-trajectory case is the statement.

Step 2.2 shows the quadratic form $\frac{x(t)^{2}}{2\ell^{2}}+\frac{\ell^{2}p(t)^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}=|z|^{2}$ is invariant; for $|z|>0$ both semi-axes $\sqrt2\,\ell|z|$ and $\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar|z|}{\ell}$ are positive, so the ellipse is nondegenerate.

Step 2.2 evaluates the endpoints $t=0$ and $t=\pi/(2\omega)$ of the quarter-period motion and step 2.1 the endpoint $t=2\pi/\omega$ of the period; the phase-space ellipse closes, so no endpoint is omitted.
The Axiom of Countable Choice is assumed in the statement and used through the evolution, fluctuation and trigonometric suppliers cited as [F1]-[F3]; steps 1.1-3.1 invoke no further choice.

boundaries.reason: Clauses (a)-(d) assert the period, the phase-space data, the invariant ellipse and the constant spreads; no biconditional is asserted.
No converse implication is asserted; the example does not claim that every periodic preparation is coherent (the scope remark of the companion page records this limit).
